<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/moving-to-0.19/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.19

This page lists each call that 0.19 moves or changes, with the old spelling and the new one.
A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below.

## The detail calls

Four calls moved to `d.detail`, with their keywords unchanged. The old names raise an `AuthorError`
that names the new home. There is no alias: one task has one spelling.

| old | new | why |
|---|---|---|
| `d.wire(a, b, wire=...)` | `d.detail.wire(a, b, wire=...)` | A path is `d.series`. A hand-wired hop is for a case no series writes (detail.md). |
| `d.net(name, *pins, kind=)` | `d.detail.net(name, *pins, kind=)` | A named net that no wire joins is a detail case. |
| `d.busbar(a, b)` | `d.detail.busbar(a, b)` | A busbar joins two fixed pins, a detail case. |
| `d.rail_bond(a, b)` | `d.detail.rail_bond(a, b)` | A rail bond joins two fixed pins, a detail case. |

A unit body's design moves the same way: `u.wire(...)` becomes `u.detail.wire(...)`. `d.earth`,
`d.mate` and `W1.core` keep their spellings.

## Grouped contacts

| before | after |
|---|---|
| one series per contact: `d.series(a.A_L1, k1.co_1.no, ...)`, and again for `co_2` and `co_3` | `q = d.poles(k1.co_1, k1.co_2, k1.co_3)`, then one `d.series(a, q.no, m1, ...)` |
| three single-pole changeover symbols | one three-pole symbol; with `selector=True` its throws face the line |

## From d.wire to d.series

Most `d.wire` calls were a current path written hop by hop. Write the path as one series instead:
it pairs the poles and takes the next free terminal or core.

A control path from rail to rail:

```python
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
k1 = d.device("K1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24")

# before: d.wire(dc.plus.pin, s1.no["13"], ...), d.wire(s1.no["14"], k1.coil["A1"], ...), ...
d.series(dc.plus, s1.no, k1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

A power path through a strip and a cable to a motor:

```python
from fransys.colours import BK

x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", *(x0[n] for n in (1, 2, 3)))
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")

# before: one d.wire per pole to X1, one W1.core per core, one d.wire per motor pin
d.series(ac, k1.main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
```

A fixed terminal, as an as-built cabinet numbers them. `x1[3]` takes the place of the next free
terminal. `x1[1:4]` is terminals 1, 2 and 3 as one three-pole element, the end excluded. A tuple puts
one terminal on each pole when they sit on different strips. A fixed terminal counts as taken, so a
strip passed whole later skips it. A tuple that runs in order on one strip raises and names the
slice to write:

```python
x2 = d.terminal_strip("X2", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
h1 = d.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
x3 = d.terminal_strip("X3", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 6)

# before: d.wire(dc.plus.pin, x2[3]), d.wire(x2[3].outer, h1.lamp["1"]), ...
d.series(dc.plus, x2[3], h1.lamp, x2[4], dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
# three phases on terminals 1, 2 and 3, and one terminal per pole across strips
d.series(ac, k1.main, x3[1:4], wire=(BK, 2.5))
x4, x5 = d.terminal_strip("X4", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4), d.terminal_strip("X5", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 4)
d.series(d.device("Q9", "DEMO-MCB-3P").element, (x2[5], x4[3], x5[3]), wire=(BK, 2.5))
```

## Behaviour that changed

| before | now | why |
|---|---|---|
| `fr.derive.takes_energy` is `True` for a `load` only | `True` for a `load`, an `actuator` and a `coil` | A motor or coil draws from its supply, so `load_limits` counts its `nominal_current_a`. A part may still state `energy`. |
| A series through a cable landed the GNYE core only when the strip before it had a `pe=` part, else it raised. | The core lands on the load's PE port. The near end is the strip's PE terminal, else earthed open. | A cable's protective core reaches its load without a hand wire (author-0044). |
| A wire to the load's PE port after such a series built a `GNYE_NOT_PE` ERROR. | It raises an `AuthorError` that names the series. | The core is already landed; a second landing is refused at the call (author-0044). |
| `d.series(j1.x1, w5, j2.x1, ...)` between two connectors raised `has no poles: name its pins`; each pin pair was a `d.wire` call. | The series pairs the two connectors' pins in pin order. A function with no line side in the middle, or at one end against a supply, a rail or a function with poles, still raises. Unequal pin counts raise and name both counts. | One derive fact orders a sideless end's pins (model-0242). |
## Channels a series takes

A series now takes a PLC channel itself. Pass the module whole and it takes the lowest free channel
(authoring.md, how channels are numbered). A script that fixes every channel, `a1.di_7`, still works.

A package that keeps the channel map of existing software checks it once. Build the package both
ways, with the channels fixed and with the module passed whole, and compare the PLC list. If the
two lists are equal, use the core form. Where they differ, keep the fixed form for those channels.

```python
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


def plc_list(fixed: bool) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """The PLC list of a two-sensor package, the channels fixed or taken by the series."""
    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    a1 = d.device("A1", "DEMO-PLC-DI-4P")
    for number in (1, 2):
        sensor = d.device(f"S{number}", "DEMO-PB-NC")
        sensor.sw.plc(fr.DI, f"Sensor {number}")
        target = getattr(a1, f"di_{number}") if fixed else a1
        d.series(dc.plus, sensor.sw, target, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    return [(r.pin, r.signal_name) for r in fr.derive.plc_channel_rows(fr.build(d).model)]


assert plc_list(fixed=True) == plc_list(fixed=False)  # equal: use the core form
```

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/moving-to-0.16-and-0.17/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.16 and 0.17

This page covers a move from 0.15 to 0.16, to 0.17, or across both. If you are on 0.16, read the 0.17 section only.
Nothing in `fr.__all__` is removed or renamed. A stored model written by 0.15 or 0.16 no longer loads.

## Moving from 0.16 to 0.17

Each change below has the old spelling, the new one and the fix.

| where | 0.16 | 0.17 | what to change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stored models | Schema 17. | Schema 18: facing is stored on every link marker. An older model raises `SchemaVersionError`. | Rebuild with `fr.build`. A layout golden or digest you keep moves by the schema stamp. |
| `PlcChannelRow` (PLC-PIN-ROWS, model-0209) | One row per channel, with `channel_designation`. | One row per pin, with `port`, `pin` and `channel_name`, and no `channel_designation`. `wired_to` holds the far ends of that pin alone. | Read `pin` and `channel_name` where you read `channel_designation`. |
| `PLC_COLUMNS` and `plc_list_rows` | Built on `channel_designation`. | `pin`, `channel_name`, `signal`, `signal_name`, `wired_to`. | Update code that picks a column by name or position. |
| `UNIT_CONNECTOR_DANGLING` (DANGLING-RETIRE, model-0219) | A `WARNING` for a spare terminal or port of a unit. | Retired: the code no longer exists. | A filter that names it now matches nothing; remove it. |
| `PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH` message | Names each channel by its module. | Names each channel by its pins, such as `-A1:1`. | Code that matches the old text must match the pin form. |

Other 0.17 changes need no code change:

- The PLC list prints one row per pin, spare pins included.
- A PLC request binds the channel it is wired to even when that channel's net holds other devices. A request of the wrong kind yields the channel to one of the right kind (model-0211).
- Several requests wired to one channel give `PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH`. Request that channel once, on one of the devices. 0.18 gives one clear finding.
- A finding message names an untagged unit by its name and revision, as its title block prints it. `unit unit` no longer appears (overview-0003).
- A coil switched by a channel pin stands under that channel (layout-0208).
- A beside branch under a host pin no longer fails with `ROUTE_FAILED`. That was a 0.16.0 regression (layout-0174).
- A terminal whose part has a protective link, such as a fuse terminal, is no longer a rail terminal (model-0215).
- PDF navigation: link markers and sheet-index rows link, viewer page labels show the sheet text, and the outline lists sheets and devices (pdf-0029, pdf-0034).
- A new package, `fransys-el`, comes in with `fransys`. A lock file gains one package (layout-0192).
- Cable page texts come out in reading order (render-0011).

## Moving from 0.15 to 0.16

### What may newly stop your build

| change | what you see | the fix |
|---|---|---|
| Stored models use schema 17 (0.15: 15) | `SchemaVersionError`: "this build reads schema version 17" | Rebuild the model with `fr.build`. A layout golden or digest you keep moves by the schema stamp. |
| `PLC_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS` is a new `ERROR` | A PLC request whose wiring ties several channels of its signal kind, none on a direct conductor, used to take the first one silently. Now it binds none. | Wire the request to one channel. The message names the request and every tied channel (model-0211). |
| `PLC_BINDING_SIGNAL_MISMATCH` message | It now names the asked kind, the channel, the channel's kind and both fixes. The severity is unchanged. | Ask for the channel's kind, or rewire to a channel of the asked kind. |
| `CABLE_PAIR_INVALID` is a new part-file `ERROR` | A `[cable_product] pairs` entry names a core out of range, a core in two pairs, a screen that is not `SH`, or an `SH` core as a pair core. | Correct the pair list in the part file. |
| `CABLE_CORE_COUNT` counts open cores | A cable with `spare` or one-ended screen cores now counts them toward its part's core count, so a warning can clear or appear. | The message names the remedy. |
| `HintError` for a group with no column | It names the group that took the devices, the loop and the `d.layout.chain` fix. It is still an error. | Apply the `d.layout.chain(...)` it prints (layout-0195). |
| `TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW` names `d.layout.page_title` | The `=F1 =F2` group-label fallback is gone. A title that fits no form is cut with "…". It stays a `WARNING`. | Give the page a short title with `d.layout.page_title`. |

These findings no longer fire, so a script that expects them changes:

- `DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS` is an `ERROR` for a `SCHEMATIC` page only when the document has no other content page. A list with rows, a `HARNESS_DRAWING` with a cable or a `BLOCK_DIAGRAM` with a sheet is enough (pdf-0033). Harness and diagram errors are unchanged.
- `UNUSED_CONTRADICTED` is checked at the unit that declares `unused=`. Declaring a passed-up interface unused on the outer unit no longer warns (model-0210).
- `LONE_CELL` skips an item box over a unit's open boundary functions (layout-0202).

### Output changes

Drawings and PDFs change byte for byte. Re-check any golden you keep.

- **Page pad.** Schematic ink keeps two wiring lanes (`PAGE_PAD`) inside the frame line, so every page moves (layout-0187).
- **Idle pins and terminals.** A connector pin or terminal that no wire inside the unit reaches is not drawn on the unit's own pages. The parent's black box keeps it, and its table still lists it (layout-0197, layout-0202). A unit with nothing left to draw adds no schematic page.
- **Connector tables.** `CONNECTOR_LIST` prints one table per connector with Pin, Net, Mate and Ends. Style, pin count and gender leave the PDF table. `connectors.csv` keeps them and gains an `ends` column (pdf-0030).
- **Boundary boxes.** A boundary box prints its landed pins, not the interface field name (model-0206).
- **Cable names.** A cable end that is a connector names it (`+C1-A1-X1`) on the cable page and in the cable list.
- **Spare cores and pairs.** `Cable.spare(...)` and a one-ended screen from `Cable.core` draw as open rows with a blank stub. A part file's `pairs` draw pair brackets. The cable list shows pairs (model-0213, layout-0207).
- **Beside chains.** `d.layout.chain(beside=...)` joins its host by one or two end nets, a one-pin box or a box head, with no marker. A box-pin run stands a grid off the pin.
- **Titles.** The title block prints the first form of `derive.page_title_forms` that fits. A strip terminal reads as its strip once ("-X1") (pdf-0028, pdf-0032).
- **Sheets page.** `PageKind.SHEET_INDEX` is in every preset, after the notes. It lists Sheet, Title and Page. Block diagram sheets read `B1`, `B2` (pdf-0031). `remove=(fr.PageKind.SHEET_INDEX,)` drops it.
- **cores.csv.** It lists every cable core with both ends, its pair and its spare mark (CORES-CSV).
- **PLC list.** Signals print in datasheet words (`DI`, `AI (mA)`, `DO (relay)`). A channel with no device and no wire prints `spare`. The CSV keeps the enum values.
- **A bridged run outside a block** takes no terminals, so its terminals join the block of their first circuit wire (author-0037).

### API names

`fr.__all__` gains no name and loses none. `fr.__version__` is new, read from `importlib.metadata`. It is not in `__all__`, so `from fransys import *` skips it.

| where | new |
|---|---|
| authoring | `d.layout.page_title(thing, text)`; `Cable.spare(*cores, at=...)`; `Cable.core` for an `SH` core earthed at one end |
| part file | `[cable_product] pairs`, and the demo part `DEMO-CBL-2X2X0.75-SP` |
| `fr.PageKind` | `SHEET_INDEX` |
| `fr.derive` rows | `OpenCoreRow`, `SheetIndexRow`, `open_core_rows`, `sheet_index_rows`, `plc_list_rows`, `connector_rows_of`, `CONNECTOR_LABELS` |
| `fr.derive` facts | `function_is_reached`, `port_is_reached`, `connector_items`, `unit_connector_items`, `signal_word`, `cores_text` |
| `fr.derive` titles | `page_title`, `page_title_forms`, `short_title`, `sheets`, `diagram_sheets`, `sheet_text`, `set_page_text`, `sheet_counter_text`, `sheet_title_text` |
| records | `layout.page_title`, `layout.open_core_wire`, `facet.open_core`, and `CableProductFacet.pairs` with `CorePair` |

`d.layout.chain(beside=)` now accepts one end net on the host and a one-pin box at the chain's end.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/moving-to-0.15/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.15

This page lists each call, name and finding that 0.15 changes, with the old spelling and the new one.
A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below. The version is read with `importlib.metadata.version("fransys")`; there is no `fr.__version__`.

## Renamed and changed names

| old | new | why |
|---|---|---|
| `text_height` in `layout.profile(...)`, an int in `G`, default 8 | `text_height_mm`, a Decimal in mm, default 1.8 | The text size is a capital height in mm (ISO 3098), not a count of grid units. |
| `min_text_mm` in `layout.profile(...)` | `min_text_height_mm`, default 1.8 | It is the floor for `text_height_mm`, in the same unit. |
| `text_mm` and `min_text_mm` on a readability page row | `text_height_mm` and `min_text_height_mm` | The same two quantities under the new names. A unit row takes the smallest `text_height_mm`. |
| `module_mm` scales symbols, gaps and text | `module_mm` sets the grid pitch only | Text and line widths are fixed in mm. Set the text size with `text_height_mm`. |
| `TEXT_TOO_SMALL` reads `text_height` and `min_text_mm` | reads `text_height_mm` and `min_text_height_mm` | The finding compares the same two values under the new names. |

## New keyword

| old | new | why |
|---|---|---|
| `fr.write(result, out_dir)` | `fr.write(result, out_dir, releases=into)` | `releases` is the folder you pass to `fr.release`. It defaults to `None`, which marks nothing. |

## The system overview

`fr.write` writes `overview.html` beside the PDFs. The page is one file and needs no network. Its switches are Colour by, Find, Parts, Select and Theme, and View inside a unit.

- **Changes** is new. It appears only when `releases` holds a release of the system, the one at the model's revision or else the previous one.
- Without `releases`, or with no release there, the page has no Changes switch.
- The Changes switch applies only to a whole-system write; a unit write gets no Changes page.

## Drawing and readability

- `d.ac_supply` no longer draws power symbols at its pins; it keeps AC rails as terminals and references.
- The readability rows have a new column, `single_contact_images_other_page`, counting the single-contact images whose one contact is on another page.

## Checks and findings

- `check` now places `overview.html` and returns its findings, so a whole-system or unit `write` meets them at the same gate. `build` does not.
- `OVERVIEW_UNPLACED` is new. It is an `ERROR`, raised when the overview placer finds no room for a view.
- The `DIAGRAM_BOX_OVERLAP`, `DIAGRAM_LINE_OFF_BOX`, `DIAGRAM_LINE_THROUGH_BOX` and `DIAGRAM_TEXT_OVERLAP` findings also check the views of the overview.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/moving-to-0.14/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.14

This page lists every `fr.derive` name 0.14 removes, and what to use instead.
`fr.derive` now holds the names a consumer needs to read a model, and every one has a guide entry. The rest stay in the workspace for layout, render and the outputs. A consumer script that used a removed name changes as below.

## Removed names

| removed | use instead | why |
|---|---|---|
| `location_node_designation` | `node_designation` | It prints any aspect node's signed path, `+` or `=`, so the name no longer says location. |
| `number`, `allocate_plc` | `fr.build(d)` | They are passes; the facade runs them. |
| `ext_usage`, `ExtUsage` | none | A migration diagnostic with no consumer use. |
| `overview_graph`, `OverviewGraph`, `OverviewLink`, `OverviewLinkKind`, `OverviewNode`, `OverviewPort`, `OverviewSignal` | none; use `fr.derive.items`, `ports` and `conductors` | The overview output is being reshaped; its graph types are not stable. |
| `box_pairs`, `BoxPair`, `draws_as_line`, `supply_share`, `connector_box_lines`, `connector_at_line_end`, `line_conductors`, `line_stub_line`, `check_side_hints` | the model records: `fr.derive.conductors`, `harness_line_ends`, `line_designation` | Drawing helpers. The model records hold the facts they read. |
| `black_box_unit`, `drawing_set_is_replica_only`, `is_black_box_item`, `schematic_functions`, `own_nodes`, `enclosing_boards`, `first_leg`, `rail_pairs`, `link_state`, `LinkState`, `changeover_throws`, `Throws`, `owned_contacts`, `Indexes`, `build_indexes` | none, or `fr.derive.functions` and `aspect_nodes` | Layout internals. |
| `profile_of` | read the `layout.profile` table of the model | The profile is a record. |
| `physical_nets`, `unused_terminals` | `fr.derive.net_of`, `fr.derive.port_is_unused` | One net, one port at a time. |
| `terminal_strips` | `fr.derive.terminal_items`, `fr.derive.unit_strips` | The kept pair covers a model and a unit. |
| `unit_items`, `unit_subtree` | filter `fr.derive.items` by `item.unit` | A plain filter of a kept table. |
| `current_revision`, `same_version` | `fr.derive.revision_history`, `fr.derive.release_order` | Compare the ordered pairs. |
| `document_unit` | `document.unit` | A field of the document record. |
| `list_context` | pass the location node you want to a row function's `context` | A value the caller passes. |
| `connector_label`, `connector_segments`, `designation_holder`, `takes_parents_designation`, `is_own_unit_root`, `is_sole_unit_root`, `standalone` | `fr.derive.item_designation`, `printed_designation` | The designation functions print the text; the helpers behind them are internal. |
| `core_colour`, `conductors_on_item` | `fr.derive.cable_rows`, `fr.derive.conductors` | The rows carry the colour; the conductors table carries the rest. |
| `cell_parts`, `cell_text`, `column_rows`, `column_values`, `pin_lines` | read the fields of a row and order them by the `*_COLUMNS` constant | Output formatting. |

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings/index.md -->

# Finding codes

Every code Fransys can emit, with severity, stage, who acts, meaning and fix, on five pages by source.

A finding's message names each thing as the drawings print it. An item reads as its designation, a port as its port designation, a wire as its ends and a tagged unit as the word unit and its tag, `unit -U1`. A unit with no tag reads as its name and revision alone, as its title block prints them. A thing with no printed text reads as its kind alone. A message never prints a `name=` key or an Id. A renamed key changes no message (decision overview-0003).

"Who acts" is one of four. `consumer`: change your design as the fix says. `part author`: the part library's author fixes the part file as the fix says. `Fransys`: a defect in layout or an output, so send the smallest model that shows it. `note`: nothing is wrong.

- [`findings-validators.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-validators/index.md): the model checks, the build, `release`, `verify` and the library load.
- [`findings-render.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-render/index.md): layout and the drawing stage.
- [`findings-pdf.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-pdf/index.md): the PDF output.
- [`findings-kicad.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-kicad/index.md): the KiCad import.
- [`findings-parts.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-parts/index.md): the part-file lint.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-validators/index.md -->

# Finding codes: validators, build and release

Codes the model checks, the build, `release` and `verify` and the library load emit. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ASPECT_CROSS_PARENT | ERROR | validators | consumer | An aspect node's parent belongs to a different aspect (function, location or product). | Move the node under a parent of the same aspect, or fix its authored parent. |
| ASPECT_CYCLE | ERROR | validators | consumer | An aspect node's parent chain loops back on itself. | Correct the parent authored on one of the looping nodes. |
| BAR_NOT_PE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A port of a `bar` function has a role other than `pe`. A bar carries protective earth only, until the copper bar drawing (owner question) is ruled. | Set `role = "pe"` on the port in the part file. |
| BASELINE_DIFFERS | ERROR | release, verify | consumer | A unit instance in the released subtree, or checked by `verify`, has a listing differing from its released baseline. | Release the nested unit's new revision, then the containing unit again, or find why its content changed. |
| BOUNDARY_NOT_IN_UNIT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's boundary function belongs to an item outside that unit's subtree. | Declare the boundary on a function whose item is in the unit, or fix the item's unit/parent. |
| BOUNDARY_UNCONNECTED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's boundary function is not connected across the unit nor declared unused. | Wire the boundary, or leave it open: `unused=` on `d.add` for one instance, on `d.device` for all. A unit alone in its design never fires it, nor an interface passed up from a nested unit. |
| CABLE_CORE_COUNT | WARNING or ERROR | validators | consumer | A cable item's core count differs from its product's core-colour count (WARNING when fewer, ERROR when more). | Wire the missing cores, mark a core you leave unused with `w.spare(colour)` (or `w.spare()` for all the rest), or correct the product's `core_colours` list. A spare or one-ended screen counts as a core. |
| CONDUCTOR_ON_UNINSTALLED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A conductor lands on an item that is not marked installed. | Mark the item installed, or remove the conductor if it is absent. |
| CONNECTOR_WIRED_WITHOUT_MATE | WARNING | validators | consumer | A conductor from outside a nested unit lands directly on its boundary connector, whose part gender is male or female (neutral or unstated passes). | Mate a plug to the boundary connector (`u.mate(plug, connector)`) and wire the plug's pin instead. |
| CONTAINMENT_CYCLE | ERROR | validators | consumer | An item's physical-containment parent chain loops back on itself. | Correct the parent authored on one of the looping items. |
| CORE_INDEX_PAST_PRODUCT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A cable core is numbered past the core count of the cable's product. | Use a core from 1 to the product's core count, or choose a part with more cores. |
| DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two items or unit instances under one parent print one designation: a tag equal to a sibling's text, or a retired or moved released one. | Give the item a distinct tag, or none. A tag a released revision reserved needs a new version. |
| DESIGNATION_MOVED | ERROR | release | consumer | An item or unit instance pinned in the previous release now prints a different designation, written or numbered. | Restore the released tag; only a new version may change it. |
| DESIGNATION_NEW_IN_REVISION | INFO | build, release | note | A new untagged item or unit instance took the next free number in a later revision. | Nothing is wrong; tag it if its number must stay fixed. |
| DOCUMENT_UNIT_UNRESOLVED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A document's `unit_name` matches no unit, or more than one. | Make the unit name unique so `unit_name` resolves to one instance. |
| EXPORT_NAME_CLASH | ERROR | build | consumer | Two different subjects (documents, items) would write to the same file name in `out_dir`. | Give the colliding units, items or documents distinct names (or locations/fragments); two instances of one release name need one document per release. |
| FILE_UNREADABLE | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file could not be read (missing file, permission error, or bad encoding). | Fix the path, permissions or encoding (UTF-8). |
| FLOAT_FORBIDDEN | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file has a bare TOML float, which the contract forbids (quote values as strings). | Quote the numeric value as a string. |
| FUNCTION_HALF_CONNECTED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A two-port coil, load, contact, switch, protection or actuator is connected at one port and open at the other. | Wire the open port, or remove the half-wired function. |
| GNYE_NOT_PE | ERROR or WARNING | validators | consumer | A green-yellow conductor is on a net that is not PE: an ERROR on a net a declared net lists, a WARNING on a net none lists (IEC 60445 keeps green-yellow for PE). | Recolour it, or connect it to the PE net and declare it with `d.earth`. |
| HARNESS_END_AMBIGUOUS | ERROR | build | consumer | Two or more ends of one cable print the same text in its drawing. | Place the colliding unit instances at distinct locations, or tag the strips apart. |
| HARNESS_HOLDS_PLC_MODULE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A PLC module sits under an item made with `d.harness`. | Build the rack with `d.rack`, so its modules print flat. |
| HARNESS_WITHOUT_TAG | ERROR | validators | consumer | A harness (marked, or with a cable child) has no tag or assigned designation, so it has no label. | Give it a tag: `d.harness(tag=...)`, or `tag=` on the item. |
| INTERFACE_NOT_BUMPED | ERROR | release | consumer | The previous released revision of this unit (the highest below this one) has the same interface string but a different boundary. | Bump the interface string if the boundary changed, or restore the previous boundary. |
| ITEM_PART_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | An item's functions or ports do not match its part's templates (missing, extra, duplicated, or differing in name, kind, role or marking). | Fix the item's authored functions and ports (or the part's templates) so they agree. |
| ITEM_WITHOUT_PART | INFO | validators | note | A non-external item has no `part`, so its functions are authored directly, not checked against templates. | Usually nothing to fix: assign a `part` to check against templates. |
| LOADS_ABOVE_LIMIT | WARNING | validators | consumer | The loads one limit bounds sum above it; none is above it alone. | If they run together, raise the limit or split the loads. |
| LOAD_ABOVE_LIMIT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A load's stated draw is above the limit that bounds it. | Lower the draw or raise the limit. |
| MATE_NOT_CONNECTOR | ERROR | validators | consumer | A mate end is not a connector or terminal (a relay coil, say). | Mate a connector or terminal. |
| MATE_PORT_MISMATCH | WARNING | validators | consumer | A mate's two functions have different port names, so some ports have no counterpart. | Example: a lettered inlet (L1, L2, L3, N, PE) mated to a numbered plug. Rename the ports to match. |
| MULTILINE_STRING | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file string contains a line break, which the contract forbids. | Use a single-line string, or TOML's escaped `\n`. |
| NET_POTENTIAL_CONFLICT | ERROR | validators | consumer | One physical net joins two declared nets that are rails of different supply potentials. | Fix the wiring or net declarations so no net joins two potentials. |
| NET_SHORTED | ERROR | validators | consumer | One physical net joins declared nets of different names. | Fix the wiring, or give the nets one name if they are one signal (same-name nets join silently). |
| NET_UNREALISED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A declared net's ports fall into more than one physical net, and no single board holds them all. Not for the PE net. | Wire the missing conductors, or remove the ports that should not share the declared net. |
| PART_LIBRARY_VERSION_CONFLICT | ERROR | library load | consumer | Two `PartLibrary` records share a name but declare different versions. | Load only one version of each named part library. |
| PE_NOT_GNYE | WARNING | validators | consumer | A single wire on a PE net is not green-yellow (an empty colour is not a finding). | Colour the wire GNYE. |
| PE_PORT_OFF_PE | WARNING | validators | consumer | A port with role PE is on a net that is not PE. | Wire the port to the PE net. |
| PLACEMENT_DUPLICATE | ERROR | validators | consumer | One item is placed more than once in the same aspect (function, location or product). | Remove the duplicate placement so the item is placed once per aspect. |
| PLC_BINDING_SIGNAL_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A PLC binding's channel does not have the signal type the request asked for (or is not a declared channel at all). The message names the asked kind, the channel, its kind and both fixes. | Rewire the request to a channel of the asked kind, or ask for the channel's kind. |
| PLC_BINDING_WIRING_MISMATCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A PLC binding disagrees with the wiring: the request or channel function is wired to a different channel or request than its binding. | Rebind the request/channel to match the wiring, or rewire it to match the binding. |
| PLC_CHANNEL_CONTESTED | ERROR | build | consumer | Two or more PLC requests of the channel's signal are wired to the same channel. The finding names the channel's pins and every request; none of them binds, and none goes to the free queue. | One channel reads one signal: keep one request, or wire each request to its own channel. |
| PLC_REQUEST_AMBIGUOUS | ERROR | build | consumer | A PLC request is wired so that several free channels of its signal tie: its net reaches them all, or all by a direct conductor. It gets no binding. | Wire the request to one channel directly, or free the other channels. |
| PLC_REQUEST_UNSERVABLE | ERROR | build | consumer | No free PLC channel of the requested signal type on the request's unit chain (its unit declares none, or every one is taken). | Add a channel of that signal type to the unit (or a parent unit), or move another request off one. |
| PORT_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two or more ports of one item print the same designation text, so a drawing or list cannot tell them apart. | Give the part's pin markings distinct names so each port prints a unique text. |
| POTENTIAL_IN_TWO_SUPPLIES | ERROR | validators | consumer | One potential name is a rail of two differently named supplies. | Rename one of the potentials, or merge the two supply declarations if they are the same supply. |
| POTENTIAL_WITHOUT_SUPPLY | WARNING | validators | consumer | A net potential no supply declares: its pins get no rank and no power symbol. | Declare the supply with that rail. |
| PRODUCT_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two items print the same product designation (location plus own label): both at one location or, unplaced, both unnumbered alike in one unit instance. | Place one item at a distinct location, or tag it. |
| RATING_BREAKING_BELOW_FAULT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A protective device breaks less current than the prospective fault at its position. | Fit a higher-breaking device. |
| RATING_BREAKING_NO_DATA | WARNING | validators | consumer | A device states breaking points, but none covers the circuit voltage or time constant. | Add a point for that voltage or time constant. |
| RATING_CURRENT_BELOW_BRANCH | ERROR | validators | consumer | A function's rated current is below the current its branch can carry. | Fit a part rated for the branch's current, or reduce the limit that sets the bound. |
| RATING_CURRENT_KIND_UNSTATED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A function's part states a voltage rating for AC or for DC only, and the function stands on rails of the other current kind. | State the missing voltage rating in the part, or use a part rated for that kind. |
| RATING_VOLTAGE_BELOW_CIRCUIT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A function's rated voltage is below the voltage that stands across it. | Fit a part rated for the circuit's voltage, or change the supply or wiring to lower it. |
| REFERENCE_DESIGNATION_DUPLICATE | ERROR | build | consumer | Two items in the function or location aspect print the same full reference designation (e.g. two unit instances at one location). | Place one of them at a distinct location so the designations differ. |
| RELEASE_FILE_CHANGED | ERROR | verify | consumer | A released file's hash differs, the folder holds a file its manifest omits, or the manifest does not parse. A CRLF-only change in a text file passes. | Restore the file from version control; a released revision never changes. |
| RELEASE_FILE_MISSING | ERROR | verify | consumer | A file its manifest lists, or the manifest itself, is gone from a release folder. | Restore it from version control. |
| RELEASE_HISTORY_UNRELEASED | ERROR | release | consumer | A history entry after the first released one names a revision with no folder under `into`, in its own version. | Remove the entry, or release that revision first. Older entries are free text. |
| RELEASE_NESTED_UNRELEASED | ERROR | release | consumer | A unit anywhere in the subtree being released (not only direct children) has no baseline folder yet. | Release that nested unit first, then release the containing unit. |
| RELEASE_NO_HISTORY | ERROR | release | consumer | The revision being released has no matching `Revision` history entry. | Add the missing entry: `history=` on `@fr.unit`, or `Design.revision(...)` for a system release. |
| REVISION_ALREADY_RELEASED | ERROR | release | consumer | The unit (or system) being released already has a baseline folder whose listing differs from the one to be written. | Bump the version or revision, or find why a frozen revision changed. |
| REVISION_CURRENT_MISSING | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's (or the project's) current revision has no matching `Revision` history entry, so a title block prints no date. | Add the missing entry: `history=` on `@fr.unit`, or `Design.revision(rev, date=, text=, created=)`. |
| REVISION_DATE_FORMAT | ERROR | validators | consumer | A revision entry's date is not in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. | Rewrite the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| REVISION_INITIALS_MISSING | ERROR | validators | consumer | A revision entry has no `created` (author initials). | Add the author's initials to the revision entry's `created` field. |
| SIDE_HINT_NO_HARNESS_LINE | WARNING | build | consumer | A `d.layout.side` hint names an interface that has no harness line, so the hint does nothing. | Remove the hint, or connect the interface through a harness line. |
| STRIP_WITHOUT_TAG | ERROR | validators | consumer | A part-less top-level item, usually a floating strip, has no tag and no class code (no terminals, or disagreeing ones). | Give it a part, a tag, or terminals of one class code. |
| SUPPLY_DIFFERS | ERROR | validators | consumer | Two declarations of one supply name disagree in current, earthing or rails, or two source declarations in fault current or time constant. | Make them agree, or give the differing declarations distinct names. |
| TOML_INVALID | ERROR | library load | consumer | A part-file is not valid TOML. | Fix the TOML syntax error named. |
| UNIT_BOUNDARY_BYPASSED | ERROR | validators | consumer | A conductor or mate crosses out of a unit at a function that is not declared that unit's boundary. | Declare it the unit's boundary, or route it through an existing boundary function. |
| UNIT_CYCLE | ERROR | validators | consumer | A unit's parent chain loops back on itself. | Correct the parent authored on one of the looping units. |
| UNUSED_CONTRADICTED | WARNING | validators | consumer | A boundary declared unused names a function that is no unit's boundary, or is connected across the unit the declaration is on. | Remove `unused=` if the function is wired, or fix the unit/function it names. |
| WIRE_COLOUR_UNKNOWN | ERROR | validators | consumer | A wire or cable-product core colour is not a recognized IEC 60757 colour code (or combination). | Use a base code, a combination of two, a base code with a core number, or shield code `SH`. |
| WIRE_ON_TWO_HARNESSES | ERROR | validators | consumer | A wire joins plugs of two harnesses. | Wire to a plug of one harness, or use a cable. |
| WIRE_ROW_UNRESOLVED | ERROR | build | consumer | A series or detail wire was written without a row, and at build end its net carries no rail of its unit, states no `source_row` and holds no PLC channel signal, or carries rails of two rows. The message names the net and the wire's two pins. | Give `wire=` on that series: a `(colour, size)`, or a size with a row table. A rail never reaches a wire across a unit boundary from its container. |

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-render/index.md -->

# Finding codes: layout and render

Codes the layout and the drawing stage emit. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CHAIN_BROKEN | WARNING | render | consumer | A connection between two "pole" cells was severed into a marker pair though its net has only those ports. | Keep the whole circuit in one function block, so no page break falls inside it ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). |
| CONNECTION_DRAWN_TWICE | ERROR | render | consumer | A connection (or net-group edge) is drawn by more than one route, or also contradicted by a cut decision. | Remove the duplicate so the connection is drawn or cut once. |
| CONNECTION_NOT_DRAWN | ERROR | render | consumer | A conductor or net-group edge is neither routed on a shared page nor cut with a marker. | Give both ends a location so layout can route or cut them; check `layout.route`, `layout.symbol_placement` and `layout.page`. |
| CONNECTION_TO_UNDRAWN | WARNING | render | consumer | A connection, net group or rail has an end whose function layout never draws. | Put the missing end's item in a drawn unit or location, or remove the connection. |
| DIAGRAM_BOX_OVERLAP | ERROR | render | Fransys | Two boxes of a block diagram or of an overview view, or a tab and a box, overlap. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DIAGRAM_CABLE_FANOUT | INFO | render | note | A cable reaches three or more boxes, so the block diagram draws a line from its first box to each other. | Nothing is wrong; split the cable only if a line per pair is not wanted. |
| DIAGRAM_CABLE_ONE_BOX | INFO | render | note | A cable's ends reach one box or none, so the block diagram draws no line for it. | Usually nothing to fix: the cable runs inside one box, or an end is an unmated plug. |
| DIAGRAM_COLUMN_TOO_TALL | INFO | render | note | A block diagram gets no page because its tallest column holds more boxes than one sheet holds; the message gives the column, its boxes and how many fit. | A known limit of the system diagram: no setting changes it. `DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS` is the error that stops the write. |
| DIAGRAM_LABEL_STRUCK | INFO | render | Fransys | A line of a block diagram or an overview view passes through a line label. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| DIAGRAM_LINES_SHARE_TRACK | INFO | render | Fransys | Two cables of a block diagram or an overview view run along one track. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| DIAGRAM_LINE_OFF_BOX | ERROR | render | Fransys | A line of a block diagram or an overview view does not end on its box's outline or tab. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DIAGRAM_LINE_THROUGH_BOX | ERROR | render | Fransys | A line of a block diagram or an overview view crosses a box other than its own two. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DIAGRAM_LOOSE_WIRE | INFO | render | note | In the system reading, a wire with no cable joins two boxes and is not drawn. | Usually nothing to fix: the unit pages show it as stubs. Put it in a cable to give it a line. |
| DIAGRAM_TEXT_OVERLAP | ERROR | render | Fransys | Two texts of a block diagram or an overview view overlap. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| DRAWING_SHORTS_NETS | INFO | render | Fransys | A page draws two nets joined that the wiring keeps apart: a stub, a wire end or a power symbol lies on, or crosses, another net's wire or symbol. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. Check first that no authored hint crowds the nets. |
| FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN | INFO | render | consumer | A function is on no current path, authored or found from the wiring, so layout placed it alone in its own column. | Wire the function into a current path (`d.series`, or `d.detail.wire` with two poles per net), or name the path with `d.layout.chain`; see drawing.md. |
| GROUP_SPLIT | WARNING | render | consumer | A group of columns is wider than one page, so layout split it between columns. | Split the block into function blocks that each fit one page ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). |
| JOIN_UNALIGNED | INFO | render | Fransys | Same-net, same-facing ports at one end of neighbouring columns could not be aligned onto one row, so layout drew references. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| KEEP_TOGETHER_UNMET | WARNING | render | consumer | An authored `keep_together` set could not be kept on one page (it does not fit, its groups sit on different drawing sets, or `break_before` is invalid). | Shrink the set, move its groups onto one drawing set, or drop the hint. |
| LABEL_UNPLACED | WARNING | render | consumer | A tag, marking or cross-reference found no free spot and sits at its default. | Use the house `text_height_mm` 1.8; give the design structure ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| LAYOUT_MISSING | ERROR | render | consumer | The model has connected functions to draw, but layout made no page for them. A function with nothing connected is drawn on no page and does not count. | Add a document so layout runs, and check the drawn location or unit holds the connected content. |
| LIBRARY_VERSION_MISMATCH | WARNING | render | consumer | A placement was laid out against a symbol library version other than the installed one. | Re-run layout (build) with the installed `electrical_symbols` version. |
| LINE_ON_OUTLINE | INFO | render | Fransys | A harness line runs along a unit outline's edge, so the two read as one stroke. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| LINK_FANOUT | WARNING | render | consumer | More than one severed link crosses between the same two pages on one net. | Join the net once with a terminal instead of severing it repeatedly between the same two pages. |
| LINK_PARTNER_UNLOCATED | WARNING | render | consumer | A signal crosses into a drawing set with no authored location, so its marker has no located prefix. | Name the drawing set's unit or location. |
| LONE_CELL | WARNING | render | consumer | A symbol has nothing connected, so it is drawn on no page; the message names the pins to wire and no page. Or a symbol stands alone on a page though its column has cells elsewhere. | Wire the named pins, or remove the device if it is not used; or move the column's cells onto one page. A unit's own open boundary functions and the item box standing under them, spare contacts and spare terminals never give it (decisions layout-0077, layout-0202 and layout-0218). |
| MARKER_UNPAIRED | ERROR | render | Fransys | A severed connection's owner or user marker is missing, or a page marker matches no severed decision. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. Check first that the cut decision and its markers agree. |
| ORDER_HINT_UNDONE | WARNING | render | consumer | An authored `keep_together` set pulled a group across an authored `order` hint, so the page order is not the one the `order` hint asked for. | Drop the `keep_together` hint or the `order` hint, or order both hints to agree; `keep_together` wins when you keep both. |
| ORDER_HINT_UNMET | WARNING | render | consumer | An authored order hint names two groups that are not on the same drawing set, so no page order can honour it. | Move both groups onto one drawing set, or drop the hint. |
| OUT_OF_CONTENT_BOX | WARNING | render | consumer | A symbol's keep-out box, label, marker box or route vertex sits outside the page's content box; the message ends " at p<page>:<cell>", with the drawing set before the page (`p<set>.<page>`) only when the layout has more than one. | Declare the supplies, wire each circuit as a current path, or split it into function blocks ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| OVERVIEW_UNPLACED | ERROR | render | Fransys | The overview placer found no room plan for one view of the system overview, so the page would have no positions for it. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| PAGE_OVERFULL | WARNING | render | consumer | A page's rows are taller than the content box; nothing is scaled. | Declare the supply, or split the circuit into function blocks ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). If it still fires, a Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| PAGE_UNDERFILLED | INFO | render | note | A schematic page whose drawn content covers under half of the content box; its message gives the share and the page reference (`+C<set>p<page>` or `(p<set>.<page>)`, from the naming pass). Nothing is moved or scaled. | No action is needed. The page is mostly empty; a larger `module_mm` spreads the content ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). |
| PIN_MAP_INCOMPLETE | ERROR | render | consumer | A symbol node has no model port bound to any of its symbol ports at all. | Add the missing model port or a `port_map`/symbol choice. |
| POWER_SYMBOL_UNPLACED | INFO | render | Fransys | No lead of up to 12 grids kept a power symbol clear of its neighbours, so it keeps one grid and may touch. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| REDUNDANT_JOG | INFO | render | Fransys | A drawn route leaves a straight line and returns to it where a straight run was free. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| REFERENCE_BOX_EXCEEDS_ROOM | WARNING | render | consumer | A drawing set has 100 or more cross-reference numbers (#n) or pages; a reference box then exceeds layout's room. | Keep each drawing set under 100 pages and 100 `#n` numbers: split the design into units. |
| REFERENCE_OFF_DOCUMENT | WARNING | render | consumer | A printed reference points to a page that no page of its own document holds, and its text prints no location, so a reader cannot tell which document to open. The message names the reference, its page and the target page. | Print both drawing sets in one document, or give the target's drawing set a location so the reference names it. |
| ROUTE_FAILED | ERROR | render | consumer | No orthogonal path on the wiring grid could be found between the two ports of a connection. | Usual causes: a redundant conductor between two points already on one net (rewire to a point already routed), or crowded geometry around the ports. |
| ROUTE_NEAR_FLAG_STUB | INFO | render | note | No path kept a wire off every link marker's stub, rail and branch (layout-0243), so it was drawn in the old room, which ignores that ink. It may touch another net's marker. The message names the page and the wire. | Send the smallest model that shows it: Fransys could not draw this cleanly. |
| ROUTE_SHORTS_NETS | ERROR | render | Fransys | A drawn route touches a port of another physical net, or two routes of different physical nets touch on the page. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. Check first that no authored hint crowds the nets. |
| ROUTE_WRONG_PORT | ERROR | render | Fransys | A route does not run between the two ports it claims to join. | A Fransys defect: send the smallest model that shows it. |
| SHEET_FORMAT_UNUSED | WARNING | render | consumer | An authored sheet format is named by no layout profile, so pages use the house sheet (or the profile's format). | Name it in the layout profile, or remove it. |
| STUBS_NOT_STACKED | INFO | render | note | Leaving-line stubs of one page whose texts meet found no free staircase (layout-0256): the room, a shape or another line was in the way. They stay as drawn and their texts overlap. The message names the page. | Move a unit or cable so the lines leave apart, or send the smallest model showing it. |
| SYMBOL_DEFAULTED | INFO | render | note | A function matched no symbol rule or choice, so it was drawn as a plain labelled box. | Add a symbol rule or choice for the function's kind or category if a real symbol is wanted. |
| SYMBOL_OVERLAP | INFO | render | Fransys | The keep-out boxes of two symbols on one page overlap. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| SYMBOL_PORT_MISSING | ERROR | render | consumer | A model port matches no port on its drawn symbol by any of the three binding rules. | Fix the part's port names, or add a `port_map`/symbol choice. |
| TEXT_CROSSED_BY_ROUTE | INFO | render | Fransys | A link marker's stub runs through a text box (a label or another marker's box). | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| TEXT_OVERLAP | INFO | render | Fransys | Two texts on a page overlap, or a text overlaps a symbol body it does not belong to. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| TEXT_TOO_SMALL | WARNING | render | consumer | A layout profile's `text_height_mm` is under its `min_text_height_mm`. Once per profile; nothing is shrunk or grown. | Raise `text_height_mm`, or lower `min_text_height_mm` if the small text is intended ([Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md)). |
| UNIT_GROUP_SPLIT | WARNING | render | consumer | A unit group is wider than one page, so layout split it; each page keeps an outline for its own interfaces. | Even the edges with side hints (`d.layout.side`), or give the unit fewer harness interfaces. |
| UNKNOWN_SYMBOL_KEY | ERROR | render | consumer | A placement's symbol key is not in the installed symbol library. | Fix the symbol key (rule, choice, or part data), or install a library version with it. |
| WIRE_NOT_ORTHOGONAL | INFO | render | Fransys | A drawn route has a non-orthogonal segment (not purely horizontal or vertical). | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| WIRE_OVER_LABEL | INFO | render | Fransys | A drawn route runs through a label's (or link marker's) box. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |
| WIRE_THROUGH_SYMBOL | INFO | render | Fransys | A drawn route runs through the keep-out box of a symbol it does not end at. | Fransys could not draw this cleanly; please report it with the smallest model |

# Finding codes: PDF

Codes the PDF output emits. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COVER_OVERFLOW | WARNING | pdf | consumer | A document's cover text plus revision table are estimated taller than the content box. | Shorten the cover or revision text. |
| DOCUMENT_EMPTY_LIST | INFO | pdf | note | A document's list page (PLC, terminal, connector, wire-label, designation, cable or BOM) has no rows and is left out. | Usually nothing to fix (pdf-0019); add records to show it. |
| DOCUMENT_MIXED_SHEET_FORMATS | ERROR | pdf | consumer | A document's pages use more than one sheet format. | Give the document (or its unit/layout profile) one sheet format for all pages. |
| DOCUMENT_NO_DRAWINGS | ERROR | pdf | consumer | A SCHEMATIC page has no drawing set and the document has no other content page, or a HARNESS_DRAWING or BLOCK_DIAGRAM page has no cable or diagram, or a drawing is missing, too large or not drawable yet: interleaved harness cables, or a block diagram whose tallest column is taller than one sheet (a known limit of the system diagram; `DIAGRAM_COLUMN_TOO_TALL` names the column). | Add the missing content, remove the page kind or shorten the texts. |
| DOCUMENT_NO_TOP_LEVEL_CABLES | INFO | pdf | note | A SYSTEM document's HARNESS_DRAWING section has nothing to draw: the model has no top-level cable. | Usually nothing to fix: add a top-level cable if one was expected. |
| DRAWING_SET_REPLICA_ONLY | INFO | pdf | note | A document's drawing set holds only black-box replicas of another unit's boundary. | Usually nothing to fix; add content if a page is intended. |
| MARKDOWN_UNSUPPORTED | ERROR | pdf | consumer | A document's cover or notes text uses a Markdown construct the PDF renderer does not support. | Rewrite it using only the supported Markdown subset. |
| TITLE_BLOCK_NOTICE_OVERFLOW | WARNING | pdf | consumer | The `notice` text passed to `fr.document(notice=)` does not fit the notice cell and would be cut. | Shorten the `notice` text in `fr.document(notice=)`. |
| TITLE_BLOCK_NO_ROOM | WARNING | pdf | consumer | The sheet format's title-block band is under the required 20mm. | Use a sheet format with a taller title-block band. |
| TITLE_BLOCK_TEXT_OVERFLOW | WARNING | pdf | consumer | A one-line title-block field (title, number, customer, revision, date, author, page title, scope or sheet counter) does not fit its cell. | Shorten the text; for a page title, set a shorter one with `d.layout.page_title`. |
| TITLE_BLOCK_UNIT_IDENTITY_MISSING | WARNING | pdf | consumer | A unit document's unit has an empty `title` or `number`, so that title-block cell will print empty. | Give the unit release a `title` and/or `number`. |

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-kicad/index.md -->

# Finding codes: KiCad

Codes the KiCad import emits. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NET_NAME_DUPLICATE | ERROR | kicad | consumer | Two or more KiCad netlist nets share a name, so KiCad would merge them on import. | Give each net a distinct name. |
| NET_SINGLE_PIN | INFO | kicad | note | A KiCad netlist net has one pin. | Nothing is wrong; wire a second end only if one was meant. |
| NODE_WITHOUT_COMPONENT | WARNING | kicad | consumer | A netlist pin belongs to an item with no footprint (or is the board's own pin), so KiCad drops it on import. | Give the item a footprint, or model the connector as a child item with one. |
| PAD_ON_MULTIPLE_NETS | ERROR | kicad | consumer | One component pad is in more than one KiCad netlist net. | Fix the wiring so each pad is on exactly one net. |
| PART_WITHOUT_FOOTPRINT | WARNING | kicad | consumer | A board item's part has no footprint, so the KiCad netlist omits it. | Add a footprint to the part. |
| REFERENCE_DUPLICATE | ERROR | kicad | consumer | Two board parts share one reference designation in the KiCad netlist. | Give each part a distinct designation. |
| UNCONNECTED_PIN | INFO | kicad | note | A pin of a board part is in no net in the KiCad netlist. | Usually nothing to fix unless a connection was meant. |
