<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings-parts/index.md -->

# Finding codes: part files

Codes the part-file lint emits, at `fr.lint` and when `fr.design` or `fr.parts` loads a library. Who acts is explained in [`findings.md`](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/findings/index.md).

| Code | Severity | Stage | Who acts | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BAR_SYMBOL | ERROR | library load | part author | A `bar` function names a `symbol`; a bar is never drawn. | Remove the function's `symbol` key. |
| BOARD_WITHOUT_PCB | WARNING | library load | part author | A part with `category = "board"` has no `[pcb]` table. | Add a `[pcb]` table with a `revision` string, or change `category` to the part's real category. |
| CABLE_PAIR_INVALID | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[cable_product]` `pairs` entry breaks a pair rule: a core is out of range, in two pairs, or `SH`, or a `screen` is not a unique `SH` core. | Give each `pairs` entry two integer `cores` in range, none `SH` and none in another pair, and a `screen` that is one unique `SH` core. |
| CABLE_WITHOUT_PRODUCT | ERROR | library load | part author | A part with `category = "cable"` has no `[cable_product]` table, or a part with another category has one. | Add a `[cable_product]` table to a cable part, or remove `[cable_product]` from a part whose `category` is not `cable`. |
| CHANGEOVER_LINK | ERROR | library load | part author | A `switched` link of a `contact_co` function joins two ports whose roles are not `common` with `break` or `make`. | Make each `switched` link of the `contact_co` function join a `common` port to a `break` or `make` port. |
| CHANGEOVER_ROLE | ERROR | library load | part author | A port of a `contact_co` function has a `role` other than `common`, `break` or `make`. | Set that port's `role` to `common`, `break` or `make`. |
| CHANGEOVER_SYMBOL_PORT | ERROR | library load | part author | A port of a `contact_co` function sets `symbol_port`. | Remove `symbol_port` from the `contact_co` port; the drawing binds a changeover by its throw roles. |
| CLASS_CODE | ERROR | library load | part author | `class_code` is not 1 to 3 uppercase letters, starts with A, I or O, or starts with D, L, V, Y or Z. | Set `class_code` to 1 to 3 uppercase letters, first letter as in IEC 81346-2, such as `K` or `QA`. |
| CONNECTOR_MARKING_REUSED | ERROR | library load | part author | Two connector functions of one part print the same label, their `marking` or else their `name`. | Give one connector function a different `marking` under `[function.connector]`, or a different `name`. |
| CONTACT_WITHOUT_SWITCHED_LINK | ERROR | library load | part author | A `contact_no`, `contact_nc`, `contact_co` or `switch` function has no `switched` link in its `links`. | Add a `links` entry with `kind = "switched"` joining its ports, or change the function's `kind`. |
| ENERGY_ON_NON_POWER | ERROR | library load | part author | A function whose `kind` is not `supply` or `load` sets `energy`. | Remove `energy` from the function, or change its `kind` to `supply` or `load`. |
| ENUM_VALUE | ERROR | library load | part author | A field typed as an enum holds a string that is no member of that enum. | Set the field to one of the values the message lists, such as a `kind` or `role` value. |
| FACET_KIND_MISMATCH | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[function.connector]` sits on a function whose `kind` is not `connector`, or a `[function.plc_channel]` on one whose `kind` is not `plc_channel`. | Change the function's `kind` to match the sub-table, or move the sub-table to the right `[[function]]`. |
| FIELD_MISSING | ERROR | library load | part author | A required key is absent: the file's `schema`, its `[part]` table, or a required field of a table. | Add the `schema = 1` line, the `[part]` table, or the required field the message names. |
| FIELD_TYPE | ERROR | library load | part author | A value has a TOML type the contract does not allow there, such as an integer for a quantity or a table where a list belongs. | Write the value as the type the message names, such as a quoted string for a rating or an integer for `schema`. |
| FIELD_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | A table holds a key the part-file contract does not name for that table. | Remove the key, or correct its spelling to a field the part-file contract names. |
| FILE_NAME | WARNING | library load | part author | A part file's name has characters other than lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. | Rename the file using only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. |
| FUNCTION_NAME_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two `[[function]]` entries of one part have the same `name`. | Give one of the functions a different `name`. |
| FUNCTION_WITHOUT_PORTS | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[[function]]` other than a `bar` has an empty `ports` list. | Add at least one entry to the function's `ports` array, or remove the function. |
| JOIN_INTO_CONNECTOR | ERROR | library load | part author | A header pin's `joins` names a port of a `connector` function. | Point `joins` at a port of a non-connector function of the same part. |
| JOIN_PORT_TWICE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two header pins of one part both `joins` the same function port. | Remove the `joins` from one of the two header pins, or point it at a different port. |
| JOIN_PORT_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | A header pin's `joins` value does not name a port of a function in this part, or is not `<function>.<port>`. | Set `joins` to `<function>.<port>` naming an existing port of another function of this part. |
| LIBRARY_FILE_MISSING | ERROR | library load | part author | The library root has no `library.toml` file. | Add `library.toml` at the library package root with `schema`, `name` and `version`. |
| LINK_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two `links` entries of one function join the same pair of ports, in either order. | Remove the repeated `links` entry. |
| LINK_PORT_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | A `links` entry's `a` or `b` is not a `name` in the function's `ports`. | Set `a` and `b` to names from the function's `ports`, or add the missing port. |
| LINK_SELF | ERROR | library load | part author | A `links` entry has the same port as `a` and `b`. | Set `b` to a different port from `a`. |
| PART_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two part files declare the same `manufacturer` and `mpn` pair. | Remove one of the files, or correct the `mpn` or `manufacturer` of the one declared in error. |
| PINCOUNT | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[function.connector]` has a `pincount` below 1. | Set `pincount` to 1 or more. |
| PLC_CHANNEL_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two `[function.plc_channel]` tables of one part have the same `channel` and `signal`. | Give one of the channels a different `channel` number, or a different `signal`. |
| PORT_NAME_DUPLICATE | ERROR | library load | part author | Two ports of one function have the same `name`. | Rename one of the ports so each port name in the function is unique. |
| PORT_NAME_SHARED | ERROR | library load | part author | Two functions of one part give a port the same name, and their printed designations would be the same. | Rename the port on one of the two functions so the printed designations differ. |
| POWER_LOSS_TWICE | ERROR | library load | part author | `power_loss_w` is set both in the part's `[rating]` and in a function's `[function.rating]`. | Keep `power_loss_w` in one place: remove it from `[rating]` or from the `[function.rating]` it repeats. |
| PROTECTION_LINK_KIND | ERROR | library load | part author | A `switched` link sits on a `protection` function, or a through link's `kind` does not fit its protection `type`. | Use `kind = "protective"` for fuse, mcb, motor_breaker and rcd, and `kind = "conductive"` for overload; never `switched`. |
| PROTECTION_TYPE_ON_NON_PROTECTION | ERROR | library load | part author | A function whose `kind` is not `protection` has a `[function.protection]` table with a `type`. | Remove the `[function.protection]` table, or change the function's `kind` to `protection`. |
| PROTECTION_WITHOUT_TYPE | WARNING | library load | part author | A `protection` function has no `type` in its `[function.protection]` table. | Add `type` to `[function.protection]`, one of fuse, mcb, motor_breaker, overload or rcd. |
| RATING_TABLE_EMPTY | ERROR | library load | part author | A `[rating]`, `[function.rating]` or `[function.operating]` table has no field. | Add at least one value to the table, or delete the table. |
| RATING_VALUE_INVALID | ERROR | library load | part author | A rating value is not a plain decimal string, is zero where a rating needs a positive value, or a breaking point list is malformed. | Write each value as a quoted plain decimal such as "24", above zero in ratings, and each breaking point with `voltage_v` and `current_a`. |
| REST_DISAGREES_WITH_KIND | ERROR | library load | part author | A switched link's `rest` disagrees with its function's `kind`: `contact_no` is open at rest, `contact_nc` is closed. | Set `rest` to match `kind`, `open` for `contact_no` and `closed` for `contact_nc`, or change `kind`. |
| REST_ON_UNSWITCHED_LINK | ERROR | library load | part author | A link whose `kind` is not `switched` sets `rest`. | Remove `rest` from the link, or change its `kind` to `switched`. |
| SCHEMA_MIXED | ERROR | library load | part author | A part file's `schema` differs from the `schema` in its library's `library.toml`. | Set the file's `schema` to the value `library.toml` names, or change `library.toml` and every file in one commit. |
| SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED | ERROR | library load | part author | A `schema` value is not in `SUPPORTED_SCHEMAS`, which today holds only 1. | Set `schema = 1`, the only supported value today. |
| SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST | ERROR | library load | part author | A `switched` link of a `switch` or `generic` function sets no `rest`. | Add `rest = "open"` or `rest = "closed"` to the link. |
| SYMBOL_PORT_WITHOUT_SYMBOL | ERROR | library load | part author | A port sets `symbol_port`, but its function has no `symbol`. | Add a `symbol` to the function, or remove `symbol_port` from the port. |
| SYMBOL_REST_MISMATCH | ERROR | library load | part author | A function's `symbol` implies a rest state (`make-contact` open; `break-contact` and `emergency-stop` closed), and its switched links, stated or implied by its `kind`, are all at the other one. | Change the `symbol`, or the `rest` of the switched links, so both name the same rest state. |
| SYMBOL_SLUG | ERROR | library load | part author | A function's `symbol` is not a lowercase, hyphenated slug. | Rewrite `symbol` in lowercase letters and digits, joined by single hyphens, such as `change-over-contact`. |
| SYMBOL_TYPE_MISMATCH | ERROR | library load | part author | A protection function's `symbol` is `fuse` or `circuit-breaker`, but its protection `type` is another one. | Make `type` match the symbol: `fuse` for `fuse`, `mcb` for `circuit-breaker`, or change the `symbol`. |
| TABLE_UNKNOWN | ERROR | library load | part author | The file has a top-level table that is neither `schema` nor a part-file table the contract names. | Remove the table, or rename it to a table the part-file contract names. |

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/examples/index.md -->

# Examples

Worked examples of whole circuits, each shown the easy way and the efficient way, and a pointer to
a full build script outside this repository. All parts are from `demo_parts`.

## A motor starter with a start/stop latch

S1 and S2 are two contact blocks: S1's break contact (`nc`) stops, S2's make contact (`no`) starts.
The power circuit runs from the three-phase supply through a breaker, the contactor's make
contacts (`main`) and an overload relay to a terminal strip. A cable carries it to the motor. The
power supply G1 takes its mains from L1 and N of the same supply. The control circuit runs from the 24 V rail through
the stop contact, a latch and the overload's break contact to the contactor coil. The latch is the
start contact in parallel with the contactor's own
auxiliary make contact.

`d.series(a, b, ...)` is the one spelling for a chain of connections, and `d.parallel(...)` puts
branches between two neighbours. The design is a plain top design: no place and no cabinet.

```python
# easy: motor starter
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", x0[1], x0[2], x0[3], n=x0[4])
g1 = d.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", g1)
q0 = d.device("Q0", "DEMO-MCB-3P")
q1 = d.device("Q1", "DEMO-CTR-3P-24")
f1 = d.device("F1", "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P")
s1 = d.device("S1", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
s2 = d.device("S2", "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC")
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(ac, q0.element, q1.main, f1.main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(ac.L1, g1.input, ac.N, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(dc.plus, s1.nc, d.parallel(s2.no, q1.aux), f1.aux, q1.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

The efficient version builds the same model. The devices come from one table of tag and part
number, so adding a device is one more line in the table.

```python
# efficient: motor starter
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BK, BU

PARTS = {
    "G1": "DEMO-PSU-24",
    "Q0": "DEMO-MCB-3P",
    "Q1": "DEMO-CTR-3P-24",
    "F1": "DEMO-OVERLOAD-3P",
    "S1": "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC",
    "S2": "DEMO-CTR-BLOCK-1NO1NC",
}

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
x0 = d.terminal_strip("X0", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
ac = d.ac_supply("400V", "230", *(x0[n] for n in (1, 2, 3)), n=x0[4])
i = {tag: d.device(tag, mpn) for tag, mpn in PARTS.items()}
dc = d.dc_supply("24VDC", i["G1"])
x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5", pe="DEMO-TB-PE-2.5")
w1 = d.cable("W1", "DEMO-CBL-4G1.5")
m1 = d.device("M1", "DEMO-MOTOR-4KW")
d.series(ac, i["Q0"].element, i["Q1"].main, i["F1"].main, x1, w1, m1, wire=(BK, 2.5))
d.series(ac.L1, i["G1"].input, ac.N, wire=(BK, 2.5))
latch = d.parallel(i["S2"].no, i["Q1"].aux)
d.series(dc.plus, i["S1"].nc, latch, i["F1"].aux, i["Q1"].coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

## Sixteen sensors to a terminal strip

Each sensor is one device, wired by its signal pin to its own terminal on a strip. The strip
takes its terminals in number order: each series that names the strip takes the next free one.
A series from a sensor's function to the strip wires its load pin `B` to that terminal. The first
sensor added lands on terminal 1, so the sensors are added from B16 down to B1.

```python
# easy: sensors to a strip
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
with d.function("SENS", "Sensors"):
    x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    b16 = d.device("B16", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b16.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b15 = d.device("B15", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b15.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b14 = d.device("B14", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b14.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b13 = d.device("B13", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b13.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b12 = d.device("B12", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b12.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b11 = d.device("B11", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b11.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b10 = d.device("B10", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b10.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b9 = d.device("B9", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b9.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b8 = d.device("B8", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b8.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b7 = d.device("B7", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b7.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b6 = d.device("B6", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b6.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b5 = d.device("B5", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b5.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b4 = d.device("B4", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b4.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b3 = d.device("B3", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b3.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b2 = d.device("B2", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b2.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    b1 = d.device("B1", "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
    d.series(b1.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

The efficient version is a list of sensor tags in the order the strip hands out terminals, and one
loop.

```python
# efficient: sensors to a strip
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

SENSORS = [f"B{n}" for n in range(16, 0, -1)]

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
with d.function("SENS", "Sensors"):
    x1 = d.terminal_strip("X1", "DEMO-TB-2.5")
    for tag in SENSORS:
        sensor = d.device(tag, "DEMO-SWITCH-2P")
        d.series(sensor.sw, x1, wire=(BU, 0.75))
```

## The whole shape of a build script

The examples above build small pieces of a design. For a real build script end to end, see
`examples/pump-station/build.py` in the public `fransys` repository, at the tag you pinned. It has its
own parts library (`example_parts`), so it cannot run as a block on
this page. It shows:

- The project and its revision history, set up once at the top.
- A cabinet unit with a second unit, the relay-interface board, mated to it through headers.
- Locations and functions built section by section: incoming supply, control supply, a PLC rack,
  and a per-pump circuit written once as a function and called for each pump.
- Several documents for several audiences from one design, then one `fr.build` and a `fr.write`
  per audience.

Consumer bugs become permanent tests in `tests/field_cases/` of the Fransys repository. Each
module's docstring states the engineering shape and the decision that fixed it.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/moving-to-0.6/index.md -->

# Moving to 0.6

This page lists every change a 0.5 consumer script or part file must make for 0.6.
Each entry gives the 0.5 spelling, the 0.6 spelling and one line of why.
The 0.5 spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.

## Imports and build

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `fr.author` and `from fransys.author import ...` | `d = fr.design("demo_parts", place="C1")`, then calls on `d` | `fransys.author` left `__all__`: the engineer surface is the one spelling. |
| `fr.build(parts, d.draft())` | `fr.build(d)` | A design holds its library, so the build needs no second argument. |
| `fr.build(parts, d.draft(), doc)` | `fr.build(d, doc)` | The same reason, with a document. |

Pass `fr.design` the generated parts module or the import-name strings that `fr.parts` takes.

## Tags and units

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `location("-C1")`, `"=M1"`, `"+X1"` | `d.location("C1", text)` | A tag is a bare key. A prefixed tag raises. |
| `unit("-A1", ...)` | `@fr.unit("A1", ...)` | A unit name is a key, with no `-`, `+` or `=` prefix. |
| unit release `interface=` | `interface_version=`; boundary values are `fn.limits(...)` | `interface` now means only the boundary marking, `interface=True`. |
| `d.add(fn, "io")`, the second argument a lowercase key | `d.add(fn, "U1")`, a printed tag; or `d.add(fn, None, name="io")` with `class_code=` on the unit | The argument is the instance's tag and key, and a container prints it: `-U1-J1`. A lowercase letter raises. |
| `d.location` called twice for one tag, order mattering | one call per tag, in any order | A location is order-free, and its text is set once. |

## Devices and terminal strips

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `item(mpn, tag=, at=, group=)` | `d.device("Q1", mpn, place=)` | The electrotechnical word is device, and its tag is the first argument. |
| `strip.terminal(3)` | `X1[3]` | A terminal strip is indexed by terminal number. |
| `strip.take(...)` | `X1[3]` or `X1.run(label, n)` | `take` had no surface spelling. Indexing and runs cover it. |
| `bridge(t1, t2)` | `X1.run(label, n, bridged=True)` | A bridge joins the adjacent terminals of one run. A run may be two terminals. |
| two parts of one MPN in a library | no surface spelling | The surface names a part by its MPN, which then names both makers. |

`d.device` and `d.terminal_strip` raise on such an MPN and name both makers.
The surface has no spelling for either part. Report the case, as a consumer case brings a form back.

## Wires

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Wire(colour, mm2, label)` | `wire=(BU, 0.75)` and `d.wire(a, b, label="L1")` | `Wire` is gone. The tuple is the one form, and the label belongs to the call. |
| `wiring(a, b, n=2)` | `d.wire(a, b, n=2)` | One spelling for a wire between two pins. |

## Groups, supplies and ids

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a terminal's `group` argument, `d.interface(fn, ...)` | the `d.function` block where the terminal is first taken; `X1.x1.limits(rating=, operating=)` | One spelling each: the block names the group, and `interface` means the boundary marking. |
| a supply with no source device | `d.dc_supply(name, plus=, minus=, voltage=)` | The pins and the voltage stand in for the source. |
| a DC supply's M rail named `M` | the rail is named `0V` | The 0 V conductor carries its potential as its name. |
| `derive.unit_ids(model)` | `sorted(fr.derive.units(model))` | It listed the keys of the units table. |
| a unit function returning a dict, `d.add(...)` returning `AddedUnit` | a `typing.NamedTuple` instance, returned by `d.add` as it is | A misspelt boundary is a type error. `fr.Run` and `fr.Terminal` type the fields that hold strips, runs and terminals. |
| `Design.unit_id` | a unit is named by its release name: `unit="pump-cabinet"` in `fr.write`, `fr.release`, `fr.verify` | There is no successor; the release name is the one name. |
| `derive.wire_label_rows` | `derive.wire_rows` and `<set>-wires.csv` | WIRE-LIST removed it on purpose (bf2d3968). |
| a per-terminal part on a strip | one strip part; a run labelled `"PE"` takes `pe=` | The strip has no per-terminal part. |

## Findings that change

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Net.potential` with no supply declared | declare the supply system: `d.ac_supply(...)` or `d.dc_supply(...)` | Without it the model gets POTENTIAL_WITHOUT_SUPPLY (WARNING) and no rank. |
| `Profile.potential_ranks` | removed: ranks follow the declared supply | A rank keyed by rail name left a rail named `L` or `12V` unranked, and its pins swapped sides. |

## Part files

| 0.5 | 0.6 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a switched link with no `rest` | `rest = "open"` or `rest = "closed"` | SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST is an ERROR. |
| `conductor = "PE"` on a pin | `role = "pe"` | A PE pin is named by its role. The pole-side `conductor` value is refused. |
| a protection `type` on a non-protection function | remove the `type` | A load ERROR in 0.6. |

A changeover contact (`contact_co`) needs no `rest` line.
Its throw roles imply it: `break` is closed at rest and `make` is open.
Its ports must still carry `common`, `break` and `make`, as in 0.5.
Only `switch` and `generic` functions with a switched link need `rest`.

## Stored models

The model `SCHEMA_VERSION` went from 2 to 7. Rebuild every stored model with `fr.build`.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/kicad/index.md -->

# KiCad

Fransys writes a KiCad netlist for each board in your model. This page shows how to import it into a
KiCad 9 board, which settings to use, and how to start a part file from a KiCad symbol.

The model is the schematic. Use KiCad for the board only: no KiCad schematic file, and no
"Update PCB from Schematic". The board gets its parts and nets from the netlist, through the PCB
editor's File > Import > Netlist. The import is a manual step.

## Get the netlist

`fr.write(result, out_dir, intermediates=...)` writes one netlist per board into the
intermediates folder, named `netlist-<board>.net`. A netlist is not an export, so it never lands in `out_dir`.

`fr.check(result)` reports the KiCad findings. Read them first. An `ERROR` (`REFERENCE_DUPLICATE`,
`NET_NAME_DUPLICATE`, `PAD_ON_MULTIPLE_NETS`) means do not import yet. Each code is in findings-kicad.md.

## Import settings

Open File > Import > Netlist in the PCB editor, pick the file, and set the dialog like this.

| Setting | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Link Method | Link footprints using component tstamps (unique ids) | Each part's id comes from the model, not from its designation. A renumbered part (`R1` becomes `R7`) keeps its footprint, position and routing. |
| Delete footprints with no components in netlist | On | The model decides what is on the board. A part you remove from the model leaves the board. |
| Replace footprints with those specified in netlist | On | The footprint comes from the part file. A footprint changed by hand on the board is drift. |
| Delete/replace footprints even if locked | Off | A lock is a deliberate choice. The import reports the locked footprint, and you resolve it by hand. |
| Delete tracks shorting multiple nets | Off | It silently removes routing. Run DRC after the import and fix reported shorts by hand. |

Never switch the link method on a board that already has footprints. Footprints imported by
reference designator carry no matching ids, so a later import by id sees every part as new.

## Import steps

1. Build the project and write it, so the netlist is current.
2. Read the KiCad findings and fix every `ERROR`.
3. In the PCB editor, open File > Import > Netlist, pick the file, and set the settings above.
4. Click **Load and Test Netlist** first. It is a dry run. Read "Changes to Be Applied" and check that
   the deletions and replacements are the ones you expect. Errors must be 0.
5. Click **Update PCB**, place the new footprints, and route.
6. Run DRC. Commit the board file together with the model change that caused it.

## Footprints that only exist on the board

Mounting holes, fiducials and logos have no part in the model. Set the footprint attribute
**Not in schematic** on each one, in its footprint properties. KiCad then leaves them alone
when "Delete footprints with no components in netlist" is on.

## Parts that are not installed

A part with `installed = False` stays in the netlist and on the board, marked do-not-populate.
The BOM report leaves it out. You do not remove it from the board.

## Start a part file from a KiCad symbol

`python -m fransys_kicad <file.kicad_sym> <symbol>` reads one symbol's pins from a `.kicad_sym`
library and prints a part-file skeleton to stdout. It has one `[[function]]` of kind `generic`, with
one port per pin.

```text
uv run python -m fransys_kicad my-library.kicad_sym DEMO-RLY-2U > parts/demo-rly-2u.toml
```

Open the new file and fill in `mpn`, `manufacturer`, `description`, `category` and `class_code`
under `[part]`. Each is an empty string marked `# TODO`. Then run `fr.lint` over the library
(see parts.md). The skeleton lints clean once those five fields are filled.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/moving-to-fransys/index.md -->

# Moving to Fransys

This page lists every change a script written for version 0.6.1 under the old name must make for Fransys 0.7.0.
Each entry gives the old spelling, the new one and one line of why.
The old spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.

## Import and alias

```text
import schematika as sk
from schematika.colours import BU
```

```python
import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU

d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.device("Q1", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
model = fr.build(d)
```

Every `sk.` call becomes `fr.` with the same name and arguments. The distribution and the import
name are both `fransys` now, so no `schematika` module remains.

## The pin line

```text
schematika @ git+<the old repository>@v0.6.1#subdirectory=packages/schematika
```

```text
fransys @ git+https://github.com/OleJBondahl/fransys@v0.7.0#subdirectory=packages/fransys
```

Pin the exact tag, as before. The repository is the public one, and the subdirectory is the
`fransys` package.

## The parts module command

| old | new |
|---|---|
| `python -m schematika parts-module` | `python -m fransys parts-module` |

The arguments are the same. Regenerate the parts module with the new command, then rebuild.
The generated file records the library's digest, which the rename does not change.

## The intermediates folder

| old | new |
|---|---|
| `.schematika/` | `.fransys/` |

Per-page SVGs and other intermediates go to `.fransys/`. Replace the `.schematika/` line in your
`.gitignore` with this one.

```text
.fransys/
```

Stored baselines verify unchanged: the rename moves no listing text.

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/drawing/index.md -->

# Drawing well

Layout draws the structure you author and invents none. This page says what layout reads, how to author a cabinet that draws readably, which numbers change its size, and which findings mean the design lacks structure.

## How layout reads the model

- **Function blocks.** `with d.function("P1", "Pump 1"):` groups the devices made inside it. Layout packs whole blocks onto pages, left to right, in order, and never reorders them to fill a gap. A block wider than a page is split between columns and reports `GROUP_SPLIT`. `d.layout.order`, `keep_together`, `break_before` and the profile's `group_ranks` set the order.
- **Page ends.** A page holds the blocks whose widths sum to the content width, 1312 grid units on the house A3 sheet. A column's width is the room it took when placed: symbols, pin labels, link markers and the column gap. In the twelve-relay example below, the first relay blocks each take 176 units, so the first page holds the supply and six relays. A page ends at the first block that does not fit, at a `break_before`, at a `keep_together` set that does not fit, or at the end of a drawing set.
- **Current paths.** Layout finds a current path where each net between two devices holds exactly two poles. A pole is the pair of pins a symbol passes current through, such as a coil or one contact. The path stands as one column, top to bottom, with straight wires. A net of three or more poles ends a path.
- **How to author a path.** Author each path with `d.series`. Hand-wired `d.detail.wire` hops form a path only while each net keeps to two poles. `d.series(a, b, c, wire=...)` wires every hop pole to pole, so its elements form a path. `d.layout.chain(...)` names a path outright, and a named path wins over discovery.
- **Block edges end a path.** A path never crosses from one function block into the next. When the two blocks land on different pages, the wire between them is cut into a marker pair and `CHAIN_BROKEN` warns. Keep each circuit inside one block. A device with two or more functions can split across blocks, a coil here and a contact there. A function of such a device, written in another block's `d.series`, draws in that block, and its coil's contact table names that page. `d.layout.draw_in` overrides this.
- **Tall paths.** A path taller than the page continues at the top of the next column, on the same sheet while there is room, then on the next sheet. The wire across each cut becomes a marker pair. The path keeps its order, and nothing runs off the page.
- **Coils on PLC channels.** A coil that a PLC channel drives stands under that channel's pin, always, whatever the row spacing. A column too tall for the page continues as tall paths do.
- **Box pins in marking order.** A box prints its pins in marking order, whatever order its wired partners stand in, and the columns hung under it follow those pins.
- **Device chains.** Some devices draw no symbol of their own, such as modules with an IN and an OUT connector. When such devices in one block are wired hop to hop, each wire alone, they form a chain. Each device then draws as one box with its wired pins only, and the chain stands as one column. A box's top pins face the device above and its bottom pins the device below, so each hop's wires run straight down. A chain starts at its end that sorts first by designation. A ring opens at its device that sorts first, and the wire that closes the ring becomes a marker pair.
- **Supplies.** A declared DC supply (`d.dc_supply`) draws a power symbol at each pin on its rails, with no wire or marker. `d.ac_supply` keeps AC rails as terminals, drawn at each pin they feed. An undeclared rail is a plain net: wires and link markers.
- **Markers.** A marker pair stands where one wire's two ends land on different pages. A net of three or more ports that is not drawn as wires gets one marker per port. A terminal is drawn at each of its wires instead. A net reference is filled with one of eight colours; every reference of the same net in the PDF has the same colour, and the text is the reference.
- **Nothing connected, nothing drawn.** A symbol with nothing connected is not drawn; its list holds it.
- **One actuator per device.** With `actuator_each_contact=False`, a manually operated device draws its actuator once, at its lead contact: the first contact its contact list prints. Its other contacts draw plain, with the device's designation and a reference to the actuator, and a contact list sits under the actuator.
- **Flat designs.** A design of devices joined by point-to-point `d.detail.wire` calls is drawn from its nets alone. Circuits that share no net fill pages one after the other. One large connected circuit with no declared supply piles onto a single page and overflows it. Declare the supply and write each path as a series (see `detail.md`).

The `draw` helper below builds a cabinet and reads its findings. The block after it builds twelve relays on
one declared 24 V supply.

```python
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


class Cabinet(NamedTuple):
    pass


Path("cover.md").write_text("# Cabinet\n", encoding="utf-8")


built = {}


def rows(model, table):
    """The rows of a layout table: `Record` values, whose fields are read by name."""
    return model.tables[table].values()


def draw(body, top=None):
    """Build one cabinet with a schematic; return its finding codes and its page count."""

    @fr.unit(
        "cab", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-01-01", text="First", by="XX",
        title="Cabinet", number="C-1",
    )
    def cabinet(c):
        body(c)
        return Cabinet()

    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    d.add(cabinet, "U1")
    if top:
        top(d)
    doc = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cab", cover=Path("cover.md"))
    result = fr.build(d, doc)
    built["model"] = result.model
    return [f.code for f in fr.check(result)], len(result.model.tables["layout.page"])
```

```python
def relays(c):
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    for i in range(1, 13):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}"):
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
        c.series(dc.plus, k.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))


declared, _ = draw(relays)
assert "OUT_OF_CONTENT_BOX" not in declared


def coil_x(model, n):
    return next(p.x for p in model.tables["layout.symbol_placement"].values() if p.key[-3:-1] == (f"F{n}/K{n}", "fn"))


assert coil_x(built["model"], 2) - coil_x(built["model"], 1) == 184
assert coil_x(built["model"], 7) < coil_x(built["model"], 1)
```

## A checklist for a readable cabinet

The pump-station example in the examples repository has this shape.

1. One unit per cabinet, and one function block per circuit: incoming supply, control supply, PLC, one block per motor starter.
2. Keep every device of a circuit inside its block, so no path crosses a block edge.
3. Declare each supply where it starts: `d.ac_supply` on the incoming terminals, `d.dc_supply` on the 24 V strip.
4. Distribute through terminal strips with named, bridged runs, and give each consumer its own terminal.
5. Wire each circuit as a path, source first: supply, protection, switching, load. Layout stands the bands in that order, with the first terminal on top and the last at the bottom.
6. Set the page order once with `d.layout.profile(group_ranks=...)`. A rank map replaces the house one whole, and an unranked block sorts last.
7. Set `hide_unused_pins=True` to leave unwired pins of box-drawn devices off the drawings. The lists keep them.
8. A terminal that only the parent wires is left off the unit's own pages; its table lists it.
9. Build, then read `fr.check(result)`. The last part of this page lists the findings that point at a missing item above.

Take each consumer's terminal inside the consumer's own block, since a terminal joins the block it is first taken in. A terminal shared by blocks adds no marker.

## Printed sizes and grid pitch

Authored numbers live on the sheet and the profile. A unit sets its own in its body, and a unit with none uses the house values. `layout-numbers.md` lists every sheet number and profile keyword with its house value and effect.

- **`module_mm`, on the sheet** (see `layout-numbers.md`). This is the grid pitch. One grid unit is `module_mm / 8` millimetres, and symbols and spacing scale with it; text and line widths are fixed in mm. The house value is 2.5. A smaller value fits more on a page, and a larger one fits less. Pitch is the reader's choice, not a fix: content that does not fit is split into function blocks.
- **`text_height_mm`, on the profile** (see `layout-numbers.md`). A style choice: the capital height in mm (ISO 3098) of the smallest text on every page kind, 1.8 in the house profile, which takes 8 `G`. A larger role prints at its ISO size (2.5, 3.5 or 5 mm) or this height, whichever is larger. Nothing shrinks text to fit. A value past what the symbols leave room for leaves tags without a place.
- **`min_text_height_mm`, on the profile.** This is the floor under the text, a capital height in millimetres: `Decimal("1.8")` in the house profile, the height the house `text_height_mm` prints. The floor changes no drawing. A profile that prints text under it gets one `TEXT_TOO_SMALL`.
- **`column_gap`, on the profile** (see `layout-numbers.md`). This is spacing: grid units between columns, 48 in the house profile. Change it to give wires and tags room, not to fit a page.

```python
def circuits(c, module_mm, text_height_mm=Decimal("1.8")):
    psu = c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)
    for i in range(1, 34):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}"):
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
            c.series(dc.plus, k.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    sheet = c.layout.sheet(
        "A3 compact", width_mm=420, height_mm=297, content_x_mm=5, content_y_mm=5,
        content_width_mm=410, content_height_mm=267, frame_columns=8, frame_rows=6,
        module_mm=Decimal(module_mm),
    )
    c.layout.profile(sheet=sheet, text_height_mm=text_height_mm)


_, house_pages = draw(lambda c: circuits(c, "2.5"))
_, compact_pages = draw(lambda c: circuits(c, "1.5"))
assert compact_pages < house_pages
```

## Which hint to use

Each hint advises the layout and invents nothing. Every name below is a method of `d.layout`.

| You want | Tool | What it does to the drawing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| These items in one column | `d.layout.chain(a, b, c)` | Stands them in one column, top to bottom, source first. |
| These groups on one sheet | `d.layout.keep_together(g1, g2)` | Moves the later groups beside the first, so they share a page when their widths fit. |
| This order | `d.layout.order(g1, g2)` | Moves `g2` after `g1`. The other groups keep their places. |
| This group starts a new sheet | `d.layout.break_before(g)` | Starts a new page at `g`. |
| This page title | `d.layout.page_title(thing, text)` | Prints `text` as the title of the pages that draw the block, function, device or nested unit. |

`d.series` is a wiring call, not a layout hint, so it has no row.

The block below applies each row to three relay blocks and reads the result.

```python
def drawn(body):
    """Build one cabinet; return the block names on each page, and the x of each named function."""
    handles = {}

    @fr.unit(
        "cab", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-01-01", text="First", by="XX",
        title="Cabinet", number="C-1",
    )
    def cabinet(c):
        handles.update(body(c))
        return Cabinet()

    d = fr.design("demo_parts")
    d.add(cabinet, "U1")
    doc = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cab", cover=Path("cover.md"))
    result = fr.build(d, doc)
    names = {handle.id: name for name, handle in handles.items()}
    pages = sorted(rows(result.model, "layout.page"), key=lambda p: (p.drawing_set, p.number))
    x = {names[p.function]: p.x for p in rows(result.model, "layout.symbol_placement") if p.function in names}
    return [[names[g.group] for g in p.groups] for p in pages], x


def blocks(c, hint=None, count=3):
    groups = {}
    for i in range(1, count + 1):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}") as group:
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
            feed = c.terminal_strip(f"X{i}", "DEMO-TB-2.5", 2)
            c.series(feed, k.coil, feed, wire=(BU, 0.75))  # a symbol with nothing connected is not drawn
        groups[f"F{i}"] = group
    if hint:
        hint(c.layout, groups)
    return groups


def coils(c, chain):
    psu = c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)
    ks = [c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24") for i in (1, 2, 3)]
    lamp = c.device("H1", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
    c.series(dc.plus, *(k.coil for k in ks), dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    c.series(ks[0].coil, lamp.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    if chain:
        c.layout.chain(ks[0].coil, ks[1].coil, ks[2].coil)
    return {f"K{i}": k.coil for i, k in enumerate(ks, 1)}


_, loose = drawn(lambda c: coils(c, chain=False))
_, chained = drawn(lambda c: coils(c, chain=True))
assert len(set(loose.values())) > 1
assert len(set(chained.values())) == 1
assert drawn(blocks)[0] == [["F1", "F2", "F3"]]
together, _ = drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, lambda hints, g: hints.keep_together(g["F1"], g["F3"])))
assert together == [["F1", "F3", "F2"]]
ordered, _ = drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, lambda hints, g: hints.order(g["F3"], g["F1"])))
assert ordered == [["F2", "F3", "F1"]]
broken, _ = drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, lambda hints, g: hints.break_before(g["F2"])))
assert broken == [["F1"], ["F2", "F3"]]
```

## What overrides what

The profile sets the numbers and the page order, and the hints then act on that order.

- **A sheet needs a profile.** `d.layout.sheet(...)` changes nothing until `d.layout.profile(sheet=...)` names it. A profile that leaves `sheet` out draws on the house A3 sheet.
- **A profile reaches only its own unit.** The top design's profile does not reach a unit, and a unit with no profile of its own uses the house numbers. A unit or the top design has at most one profile, and a second one with other numbers raises `AuthorError`.
- **A keyword left out keeps its house value.** A rank map you give replaces the house one whole.
- **`order` beats `group_ranks`.** The ranks sort the blocks first, then each `order` hint moves blocks from that order.
- **`keep_together` beats `order`.** It runs after the order hints, pulls its groups next to the first, and reports `ORDER_HINT_UNDONE` when that reverses an `order` hint.
- **`break_before` on a later group of a `keep_together` set** leaves the set unkept and reports `KEEP_TOGETHER_UNMET`. On the set's first group it changes nothing.
- **Order hints that form a cycle** make the build raise `fr.AuthorError` naming the cycle.
- **A chain names a box-drawn function only at its head or its tail.** A PLC channel or a supply output stands there and anchors the path at its pin. In the middle the build raises `fr.AuthorError` that says where box-drawn functions may stand.

```python
def compact_sheet(scope):
    return scope.layout.sheet(
        "A3 compact", width_mm=420, height_mm=297, content_x_mm=5, content_y_mm=5,
        content_width_mm=410, content_height_mm=267, frame_columns=8, frame_rows=6,
        module_mm=Decimal("1.5"),
    )


def numbers(c):
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    for i in range(1, 34):
        with c.function(f"F{i}", f"Relay {i}"):
            k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
            c.series(dc.plus, k.coil, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))

assert draw(lambda c: (numbers(c), c.layout.profile(sheet=compact_sheet(c))))[1] < house_pages

ranked = lambda hints, g: hints.profile(group_ranks={"F3": 1, "F2": 2, "F1": 3})
assert drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, ranked))[0] == [["F3", "F2", "F1"]]


def ranked_then_ordered(hints, g):
    ranked(hints, g)
    hints.order(g["F1"], g["F3"])


assert drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, ranked_then_ordered))[0] == [["F2", "F1", "F3"]]


def kept_and_ordered(hints, g):
    hints.keep_together(g["F1"], g["F3"])
    hints.order(g["F2"], g["F3"])


assert drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, kept_and_ordered))[0] == [["F1", "F3", "F2"]]


def kept_and_broken(hints, g):
    hints.keep_together(g["F1"], g["F2"])
    hints.break_before(g["F2"])


unkept = lambda c: blocks(c, kept_and_broken)
assert "KEEP_TOGETHER_UNMET" in draw(lambda c: unkept(c))[0]
assert drawn(unkept)[0] == [["F1"], ["F2", "F3"]]


def cycle(hints, g):
    hints.order(g["F1"], g["F2"])
    hints.order(g["F2"], g["F1"])


top_only = draw(lambda c: numbers(c), top=lambda d: d.layout.profile(sheet=compact_sheet(d)))[1]
assert top_only == house_pages

try:
    draw(lambda c: (c.layout.profile(text_height_mm=Decimal("1.8")), c.layout.profile(text_height_mm=Decimal("2.0"))))
except Exception as error:
    assert type(error).__name__ == "AuthorError"
else:
    raise AssertionError("a second profile must raise")

try:
    drawn(lambda c: blocks(c, cycle))
except Exception as error:
    assert type(error).__name__ == "AuthorError" and "cycle" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("an order cycle must raise")
```

## Findings that mean missing structure

- **`FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN`.** No current path reaches the function, so it stands alone in a column. A box-drawn device, such as a power supply or a lamp, has no pole of its own. It stands in a path only when a path ends on it. A lamp wired straight across two rails is on none, and wired after a contact it ends that contact's path. Many of these in one unit mean many devices hang on no path.
- **`LABEL_UNPLACED`.** A tag, marking or cross-reference found no free place. A `text_height_mm` above the house value is one cause. Put it back to 1.8.
- **`CHAIN_BROKEN`.** A path was cut by a page break between two blocks. Keep the circuit in one block.
- **`PAGE_OVERFULL` and `OUT_OF_CONTENT_BOX`.** A circuit is too big for its page. Declare its supply, wire it as paths, or split it into blocks. Else send the smallest model. `PAGE_PAD` frames the ink.
- **Readability.** Five findings tell you whether the printed pages can be read. `TEXT_TOO_SMALL` says the profile prints text under `min_text_height_mm`. `PAGE_UNDERFILLED` says a page's content covers under half of its content box. `TEXT_OVERLAP`, `WIRE_OVER_LABEL` and `LABEL_UNPLACED` say text collides with text or a wire, or has no place. Those two are INFO: Fransys defects, report with the smallest model.

The next block counts the first two. Lamps wired across the rails stand alone, lamps after a contact do not, and a text height of 24 leaves tags without a place.

```python
def lamps(c, after_contact):
    psu = c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24")
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", psu.output)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
        h = c.device(f"H{i}", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
        if after_contact:
            c.series(dc.plus, k.co_1.no, h.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
        else:
            c.series(dc.plus, h.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))


across, _ = draw(lambda c: lamps(c, after_contact=False))
after, _ = draw(lambda c: lamps(c, after_contact=True))
assert across.count("FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN") > after.count("FUNCTION_UNPLACED_IN_COLUMN")

big_text, _ = draw(lambda c: circuits(c, "2.5", text_height_mm=Decimal("5.4")))
assert "LABEL_UNPLACED" in big_text
```

The numbers behind the readability findings are in `fr.readability`: `readability.md`.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/readability/index.md -->

# Reading the pages as numbers

`fr.readability(result)` returns a `ReadabilityReport` with the numbers behind the findings: one `ReadabilityPage` row for each schematic page in `.pages` and one `ReadabilityUnit` row for each unit in `.units`. The three types are also in `fr.derive`. The same model gives equal rows, so compare a unit between revisions by its rows. It writes no file and `fr.write` does not emit it. It lays the schematic out again. Only a drawing set that some document prints gets rows. The look findings (`PAGE_UNDERFILLED`, `WIRE_OVER_LABEL`, `TEXT_OVERLAP`, `LONE_CELL`) skip the other sets too.

The findings these numbers back are in `drawing.md`.

- **`drawing_set`, `number` and `unit`.** The page as printed in the corner, and the unit it belongs to (`None` for the design's own pages).
- **`text_height_mm` and `min_text_height_mm`.** The smallest printed capital height in mm and its floor. Change nothing when `text_height_mm` is at or over the floor. When under, raise `text_height_mm` on the profile.
- **`fill_percent`.** The share of the page's content box the drawing covers, in whole percent. A low number is a mostly empty page with small text. Merge its group into the page before it, or drop a `break_before`.
- **`wire_crossings`.** How often a wire or a fan-out leg runs across a wire of another net or another cable's core line or leg. A cable's own legs and line meet by design. A high number means a tangled page. Order the groups with `order`, or put the crossing nets on separate pages.
- **`wire_bends`, `wire_length_mm`.** The direction changes and the total length in mm of every conductor line drawn on the page: routed wires, straight power leads and fan-out legs. A harness or cable line is not counted. Many bends or a long total mean a winding page: a shorter run or a nearer neighbour reads better. They are numbers to compare between revisions, not a target the layout optimises.
- **`struck_labels`.** Texts a wire runs through (`WIRE_OVER_LABEL`). It is INFO: report it with the smallest model.
- **`text_overlaps`.** Texts that overlap each other or a symbol they do not belong to (`TEXT_OVERLAP`).
- **`lone_cells`.** Symbols standing alone on a page (`LONE_CELL`). Keep the circuit in one block, or wire the symbol.
- **`contact_images`, `contact_image_targets` and `single_contact_images`.** The coil images on the page, the contacts they list and the images that list one. Many single images mean a relay used for one contact: a plain wire may read better.
- **`single_contact_images_other_page`.** The single images whose one contact is on another page, a part of `single_contact_images`. Such an image points off the page, so it reads less well than one beside its contact.
- **`stars`, `star_branches` and `single_branch_stars`.** The net references on the page, the branches they name on other pages and the references that name one. Many on several pages mean the net is cut across pages. Declare the supply so it is drawn once, or keep the net's ends together.
  A star can also stand on one page, and then it is no cut. A pin with two or more wires takes a reference for each end. One breaker pin feeding two coils gives each of the three ports a marker naming the other two. A wire that would turn back round its own device is a marker pair too. A contact above a box, with both pins wired to the box's top pins, is one. For the first, distribute through a terminal strip with a named, bridged run (checklist item 4). A bridged three-terminal run took one page from 2 stars to 1.
- **`contacts_not_drawn`.** The contact-image entries that print `N/A`: a contact no conductor reaches. Information only, with no finding, since `N/A` is how a contact with nothing drawn prints. Many on one coil mean a relay bought for contacts the circuit does not use.
- **`references_off_document`.** References on the page to a page of another document that print no location. A reader cannot tell which document to open. `REFERENCE_OFF_DOCUMENT` is a warning that names the reference and its page. The bar is 0. Print both drawing sets in one document. Or give the target's drawing set a location, so the reference names it. A reference that prints its location, such as `+FLDp1:2A`, is correct.
- **`page_cuts`.** The wires of two ports cut at a page break, each naming one other page. Keep the two ends in one block, or add a terminal where the circuit changes page.

A reference text reads `p<n>:<cell>` for sheet n of the reference's own drawing set. It reads `p<set>.<page>:<cell>` for a sheet of another set. A net reference adds the net's number, `#<n>`, then its first target. That target is a terminal of the net when it has one, else the first other end in reading order. A marker with more than two other ends prints that target and `+k` for the k others. A contact no conductor reaches prints `N/A` in place of a position. Pole-linked contacts of one item in one row print one back reference to the coil. The coil's table lists every contact.

`report.loose_symbols` counts the symbols of the whole build that no page draws, those with nothing connected. No page row carries it. A unit row counts its own loose symbols, adds up the counts of its pages and their wire length, and takes the smallest `text_height_mm` and `fill_percent` and the highest `min_text_height_mm`. Its `pages` is the page count.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

import fransys as fr
from fransys.colours import BU


class Cabinet(NamedTuple):
    pass


Path("cover.md").write_text("# Cabinet\n", encoding="utf-8")


@fr.unit(
    "cab", revision=1, interface_version=1, date="2026-01-01", text="First", by="XX",
    title="Cabinet", number="C-1",
)
def measured(c):
    dc = c.dc_supply("24VDC", c.device("G1", "DEMO-PSU-24").output)
    for i in range(1, 6):
        k = c.device(f"K{i}", "DEMO-RLY-2CO-24")
        h = c.device(f"H{i}", "DEMO-LAMP-24")
        c.series(dc.plus, k.co_1.no, h.lamp, dc.minus, wire=(BU, 0.75))
    return Cabinet()


d = fr.design("demo_parts")
d.add(measured, "U1")
doc = fr.document(fr.DocumentPreset.CABINET_SCHEMATIC, "cab", cover=Path("cover.md"))
report = fr.readability(fr.build(d, doc))
assert report.pages
assert all(page.text_height_mm >= page.min_text_height_mm for page in report.pages)
assert sum(unit.pages for unit in report.units) == len(report.pages)
```

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/overview/index.md -->

# The system overview

`overview.html` is one file that `fr.write(result, out_dir)` puts beside the PDFs. It needs no network and no server: open it in a browser. This page says how to read it.

The page starts at the system: each cabinet unit is a box, each cable a line. Double-click a unit, or select it and press Enter, to open it; the crumbs above the drawing and "Up one level" go back. A unit opens as its function groups, as all devices with strips drawn through, as lanes when it has them, or as plain boxes: pick one under "View". A stub opens its far side in place.

- **Colour by** a unit, a function group, an item kind or a location. The legend counts the boxes of the level shown; click a class to hide it, and a chip above the drawing brings it back.
- **Find** an item by designation in the search box; Enter opens its level and selects it.
- **Parts** on the left lists every item as a tree; the boxes hide an item and what it holds.
- **Select** a box or line to dim the rest and list its facts and the signals through it on the right. An item drawn on a PDF page lists its pages, each a link to that page. Keep the HTML and the PDFs together in the folder `write` made.
- **Theme** is light, dark or your system's. The address holds the whole view, so Back, Forward and a copied link return to it.

With no document in the build there is no PDF, so the page has no links. The page holds no internal id, so a rename that changes no printed text changes no byte of it.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/AGENTS/index.md -->

# For coding agents

The official Fransys documentation is the site, one version per release. Read it there, never in the
installed package folder (`site-packages/fransys/`). Paste this block into your project's
`CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` so every agent that works on the project finds it:

```markdown
## Fransys documentation

- The official documentation is https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/ .
- Take the version from the installed package: `importlib.metadata.version("fransys")` is `X.Y.Z`.
- Start at https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/X.Y.Z/llms.txt. Its `llms-full.txt` is the whole guide in one file.
- Read a page as Markdown at its URL plus `index.md`, such as https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/X.Y.Z/guide/index.md.
- Import only `fransys`. Write with the calls the guide index names under "Which call first".
- Do not read `site-packages/fransys/`. Its guide is an offline fallback for when the site is unreachable.
```

The part-file format is in
[the part-file contract](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/X.Y.Z/contracts/part-file/index.md), at the same version path.
For type checking a design script, read [Type checking](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/guide/keywords/index.md#type-checking).

## Offline fallback

Without network access the guide ships inside the installed package. Find the version you have
installed with `importlib.metadata.version("fransys")`. Find the guide folder with the standard
resource-loading call for package data, in Python:

```
importlib.resources.files("fransys").joinpath("guide")
```

Read `index.md` next. This file restates no API. The guide pages and the package's own docstrings
are the reference.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/contracts/part-file/index.md -->

# Part-file contract

Version 1. Parts are data, not code: TOML files in a data package that the loader reads and the
lint checks.

## Purpose and audience

This contract is for someone writing a part library without reading Fransys's source. A part
library is a Python data package of TOML files and no code. This document is enough to write one that
`fransys_parts.load` and `fransys_parts.lint` accept.

## Library layout

```
<library-package>/
  __init__.py
  library.toml
  parts/
    relay-2co-24vdc.toml
    terminal-feedthrough-2_5.toml
    cable-4g1_5.toml
    ...
```

- `__init__.py` carries a one-line docstring and no code: it only makes the directory importable
  by `load(package)`.
- `library.toml` sits at the package root and describes the library as a whole.
- Every part lives in its own file under `parts/`. The loader ignores the filename; a lowercased,
  hyphenated MPN or short description is expected.
- TOML is read with stdlib `tomllib` and `parse_float=Decimal`. No other file format is
  accepted.

## `library.toml` fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | integer | The part-file schema version this library is written against. See "Versioning" below |
| `name` | string | The library's name, recorded on the model so a drawing states which library it used |
| `version` | string | The library's own version, recorded alongside `name` |
| `description` | string | Free text, not read by the loader |

## Part file tables

Every part file carries `schema = 1` at the top, then the tables below. Fields named here match
the model's records (the core kinds and the facets); a field not listed there is out of contract.

Any field below typed as "a `<Name>` value" takes the string value of a member of that enum in
`fransys_model.vocab.enums`. That module is the authority: the allowed-values lists in this
contract are copied from it and can go stale, the module cannot.

### `[part]`

One per file. Maps to the model's `Part`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mpn` | string | Manufacturer part number. The only home of this fact once loaded |
| `manufacturer` | string | |
| `description` | string | |
| `category` | string | A `PartCategory` value: `"electromechanical"`, `"protection"`, `"terminal"`, `"cable"`, `"connector"`, `"plc_module"`, `"board"`, `"generic"` |
| `class_code` | string | 1 to 3 uppercase letters, IEC 81346-2:2019, seeding numbering, e.g. `"K"`, `"Q"`, `"QA"`, `"X"`, `"W"`. The first letter is one of `B C E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U W X`; A, I and O are forbidden and D, L, V, Y and Z reserved (parts lint) |
| `operated_by` | string | Optional. An `OperatedBy` value, what operates the part's contacts as sold: `"push"`, `"mushroom"`, `"turn"`, `"position"` (parts-0020). A head sold apart from its blocks states it and has no function; its blocks join it with `parent=` |

### `[[function]]`

Zero or more per file, one array entry per function the part has. Maps to the model's
`FunctionTemplate`, with nested `ports` mapping to `PortTemplate` and nested `links` mapping to
`InternalLink`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Function name, stamped onto every instance, e.g. `"coil"`, `"co_1"` |
| `kind` | string | A `FunctionKind` value: `"coil"`, `"contact_no"`, `"contact_nc"`, `"contact_co"`, `"protection"`, `"switch"`, `"terminal"`, `"connector"`, `"plc_channel"`, `"supply"`, `"load"`, `"sensor"`, `"actuator"`, `"generic"`, `"bar"` |
| `symbol` | string | Optional. Symbol key: a lowercase, hyphenated slug naming a symbol in `electrical-symbols`. A function with no `symbol` gets no authored `layout.symbol_choice`, and the layout engine's rules by kind apply |
| `energy` | string | Optional, on a supply or load function only: `"in"` or `"out"`. Default: load in, supply out. Any other kind fails lint (`ENERGY_ON_NON_POWER`) |
| `ports` | array of tables | See below. At least one entry, except a `bar` cut to length (below) |
| `links` | array of tables | See below. Optional; omit for a function with no internal connectivity |

A `bar` writes one port per screw, role `"pe"`; one cut to length writes none, and each landing makes a screw. It takes no `symbol` (`BAR_SYMBOL`): a bar is never drawn.

`ports` entries:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The part's own terminal marking, e.g. `"13"`, `"A1"`. Unique within the part, except pins of connectors that print a label. Name a terminal as the device prints it (`IN1+`, `OUT-`); where printed names repeat on the part, by its function, numbered (`L`, `N`, `PE`, `24V1`, `GND1`, `S24V`, `F24V1`) (owner 2026-09-26, parts-0005) |
| `role` | string | A `PortRole` value: `"generic"`, `"internal"`, `"external"`, `"pe"`, or a throw role `"common"`, `"break"` (closed at rest), `"make"` (closed when operated). Every port of a `contact_co` function takes a throw role, whatever its pin name (`CHANGEOVER_ROLE`, decisions model-0091, parts-0007) |
| `symbol_port` | string | Optional. The role-named port of `symbol` this port maps to, e.g. `"in"`, `"out"`. A port with no `symbol_port` keeps its own name. A `symbol_port` on a function with no `symbol` is a lint error (`SYMBOL_PORT_WITHOUT_SYMBOL`). A `contact_co` port takes none: the drawing binds a changeover by its throw roles (`CHANGEOVER_SYMBOL_PORT`) |
| `marking` | string | Optional. What a drawing prints on this pin, when it differs from `name`. Omit it to print `name`; write `""` to print nothing |
| `side` | string | Optional: `"line"` or `"load"`; else the marking fills it (parts-0010). A two-port function that a series passes through needs it when its marking gives no side |
| `conductor` | string | Optional: `"L1"`, `"L2"`, `"L3"`, `"N"`, `"L+"`, `"L-"`, `"M"`; not `"PE"` (use `role = "pe"`), filled likewise |
| `source_row` | string | Optional. The wiring row a wire on this pin takes, a `WiringRow` value: `"DC_SUPPLY"`, `"DC_GROUND"`, `"DC_CONTROL"`, `"DC_SIGNAL"`, `"AC_L1"`, `"AC_L2"`, `"AC_L3"`, `"AC_N"`, `"AC_CONTROL"`. Omit it to let the build resolve the row from the pin's net (model-0260); a `wire=` row map overrides it |

`links` entries:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | string | A `name` from this function's `ports` |
| `b` | string | A `name` from this function's `ports` |
| `kind` | string | A `LinkKind` value: `"conductive"`, `"switched"` or `"protective"` |
| `rest` | string | Optional, `switched` only: `"open"` or `"closed"` |

A `protective` link is a fuse or breaker, closed in service. It ends the physical net but not the
supply rail (decision model-0122). An overload's main path is `conductive`.

In a `contact_co` function, every `switched` link joins the `common` port to a `break` or a
`make` port (`CHANGEOVER_LINK`).

Rest state (decision parts-0008): a `contact_no` or `contact_nc` may omit `rest` and must agree
if it writes it. A `switch` or `generic` function must write `rest`. Lint, all
`ERROR`: `SWITCHED_LINK_WITHOUT_REST`, `REST_DISAGREES_WITH_KIND`, `REST_ON_UNSWITCHED_LINK`,
`CONTACT_WITHOUT_SWITCHED_LINK`, and `SYMBOL_REST_MISMATCH` (`make-contact` is open and
`break-contact` and `emergency-stop` closed).

### `[[supply]]`

Zero or more per file. Maps to the model's `supply` facet, which allows many per part.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `supplier` | string | |
| `supplier_part_number` | string | |
| `note` | string | Optional |

### `[footprint]`

At most one per file. Maps to the model's `footprint` facet (subject: `Part`).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `library` | string | A KiCad footprint library name |
| `name` | string | The footprint's name within that library |

Written into the KiCad netlist as `library:name` (design section 7). `fransys_kicad` writes
this reference; it does not read the footprint itself.

### `[cable_product]`

At most one per file. Maps to the model's `cable_product` facet (subject: `Part`).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `core_count` | integer | The author's checksum: the lint's `CABLE_CORE_COUNT` compares it with `core_colours`. The model stores no count; it reads `len(core_colours)` (model-0082) |
| `core_colours` | array of strings | One entry per core, in core index order, e.g. `["BN", "BK", "GY", "GNYE"]`. Each is an IEC 60757 colour code: a base code, two base codes joined (`GNYE`), a base code with a number (`BK1`), or `SH` for a shield (model-0070); anything else is an ERROR |
| `gauge_mm2` | string | Cross-section in mm², read as `Decimal` |
| `shielded` | boolean | |
| `pairs` | array of tables, optional | One `{ cores = [a, b], screen = n }` per twisted pair: two core numbers, and its `SH` core if it has one. The drawing labels the pairs P1, P2 (CC8) |

`CABLE_PAIR_INVALID` (ERROR) refuses a core out of range or in two pairs. It also refuses a pair core that is `SH`, and a screen that is not `SH` or is named twice.

### `[function.protection]`

A `protection` function names its device in `type`: `"fuse"`, `"mcb"`, `"motor_breaker"`,
`"overload"` or `"rcd"`. The loader writes it to `FunctionTemplate.protection_type`, null when absent.
Lint: `PROTECTION_WITHOUT_TYPE` (`WARNING`), `PROTECTION_TYPE_ON_NON_PROTECTION`
(`ERROR`), `PROTECTION_LINK_KIND` (`ERROR`, a `switched` link or a kind that does not fit the type)
and `SYMBOL_TYPE_MISMATCH` (`ERROR`, a symbol of another type).
A through link is `protective` for fuse, mcb, motor_breaker and rcd, and `conductive` for overload.

Default symbols (layout-0105). A `symbol` on the part or a layout choice always wins.

| Function | Symbol |
|---|---|
| switch operated by push, open / closed at rest | `push-button` / `push-button-break` |
| switch operated by mushroom, closed at rest | `emergency-stop` |
| switch operated by turn, open / closed at rest | `selector-make` / `selector-break` |
| switch operated by position, open / closed at rest | `position-switch-make` / `position-switch-break` |
| switch, open at rest | `make-contact` |
| switch, closed at rest | `break-contact` |
| `fuse` | `fuse` |
| `mcb`, `motor_breaker` | `circuit-breaker` |
| `overload` | `thermal-overload`, one box per pole |
| `rcd` | `rcd` |
| protection with no type | `circuit-breaker` |

A switch is operated by its own part's `operated_by`, else by the nearest holder's (layout-0220, model-0222). An emergency stop states `operated_by = "mushroom"`.

Poles (F4, model-0128). A pole is a switched or protective link, or a protection function's
conductive link. Poles run in natural marking order, line side on top; no side fact keeps marking order.

The `[function.connector]` table is in `part-file-connectors.md`.

### `[function.plc_channel]`

A sub-table of the `[[function]]` entry it describes (P1): a multi-channel PLC module part has
one `[[function]]`, and one `[function.plc_channel]`, per channel. Maps to the model's
`plc_channel` facet (subject: `FunctionTemplate`).

```toml
[[function]]
name = "di_3"
kind = "plc_channel"
ports = [{ name = "3", role = "generic" }]

[function.plc_channel]
signal = "di"
channel = 3
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `signal` | string | A `SignalType` value: `"di"`, `"do"`, `"ai_current"`, `"ai_voltage"`, `"ao_current"`, `"ao_voltage"`, `"rtd"`, `"relay"` |
| `channel` | integer | Channel number on the module |

### `[rating]`, `[function.rating]` and `[function.operating]`

`[rating]` (top level, at most one per file) is the part's own rating, e.g. a cable's rated
voltage or a fuse link in its holder; it maps to the `part_rating` facet (subject: `Part`).
`[function.rating]` and `[function.operating]` are sub-tables of a `[[function]]` entry (P1); they
map to the `rating` and `operating` facets (subject: `FunctionTemplate`). `power_loss_w` is the heat given off at the rated load. `resistance_ohm`, `nominal_power_w` and
`nominal_current_a` are stated at `nominal_voltage_v`. No check reads the first two (model-0125, parts-0009).
A part states `power_loss_w` once, in `[rating]` or per function: both is `POWER_LOSS_TWICE` (`ERROR`).
A function takes its template's rating, else its part's, as a whole record: a template rating with only an AC value
hides the part's DC value (decisions model-0079, parts-0004).

```toml
[[function]]
name = "coil"
kind = "coil"
ports = [{ name = "A1", role = "generic" }, { name = "A2", role = "generic" }]

[function.rating]
voltage_ac_v = "250"
```

| Table | Fields, all optional |
|---|---|
| `[rating]`, `[function.rating]` | `voltage_ac_v`, `voltage_dc_v`, `current_ac_a`, `current_dc_a`, `min_breaking_current_a`, `power_loss_w`, `breaking_ac`, `breaking_dc` |
| `[function.operating]` | `voltage_ac_v`, `voltage_dc_v`, `nominal_voltage_v`, `max_voltage_v`, `min_voltage_v`, `capacity_ah`, `max_current_ac_a`, `max_current_dc_a`, `resistance_ohm`, `nominal_power_w`, `nominal_current_a`, `fault_current_ac_a`, `fault_current_dc_a`, `fault_time_constant_ms` |

A breaking list is non-empty. A `breaking_dc` point may add `time_constant_ms`:

```toml
breaking_dc = [{ voltage_v = "1000", current_a = "15000", time_constant_ms = "15" }]
```

`min_breaking_current_a` marks a partial-range fuse (an aBat link): the lowest current it
breaks. It bounds no continuous current. `max_current_ac_a` and `max_current_dc_a` are a source's continuous current limit, charging included (decision model-0088).

Every value is a string in plain decimal notation (digits with an optional fraction), read as
`Decimal`. A rating value is above 0; a `[function.operating]` value
may also be 0 (`"0"`, `"0.0"`: a source's minimum voltage), decision parts-0006. A bare TOML
float is `FLOAT_FORBIDDEN` and an integer is `FIELD_TYPE`. The lint refuses, as `ERROR`, a table
with no field (`RATING_TABLE_EMPTY`) and a value outside those rules, negative or not plain
(`RATING_VALUE_INVALID`). The `RATING_VOLTAGE_BELOW_CIRCUIT` and
`RATING_CURRENT_BELOW_BRANCH` checks read a rating. Of the operating values, only `max_current_*`, `nominal_current_a` and `fault_*` are read. A part
with no current rating limits no branch (model-0088).

### `[pcb]`

At most one per file. Maps to the model's `pcb` facet (subject: `Part`); marks a board part.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `revision` | string | |

## Rules

- **No floats.** Every table is read with `parse_float=Decimal`. A bare TOML float (`1.5`
  unquoted) is `FLOAT_FORBIDDEN` wherever it sits in the file; write it as a string (`"1.5"`).
- **Quantities are strings read as `Decimal`.** `gauge_mm2` is the example.
- **Lengths are integer millimetres.** A length field is a plain TOML integer.
- **The symbol key is a slug.** `symbol` is lowercase and hyphenated (`"operating-device"`,
  `"change-over-contact"`), naming a key in `electrical-symbols`. `fransys_parts` checks the
  slug's shape only; the layout engine reports an unknown symbol or unbound port.
- **`symbol_port` names a role of the symbol, not a marking of the part.** The symbol knows
  shapes and calls its ports by role (`in`, `out`, `com`, `nc`, `no`); the part knows markings
  and calls the same ports by what is printed on it. `ports.marking` overrides what is printed (design section 6). A changeover binds by its throw roles.
- **Footprint is `library:name`.** Never a bare name.
- **No multi-line strings.** The loader finds a record's line by scanning the file text once for
  table headers (decision parts-0001); a multi-line string could hide a header. No string value
  may contain a line break (lint: `MULTILINE_STRING`, checked on the parsed values).
- **A file that cannot be read is a finding, not a crash.** An unreadable or non-UTF-8 part file is
  `FILE_UNREADABLE`; `lint` and `load_path` still check every other file.

## Worked examples

The demo part library, `examples/demo-parts/`, is the worked example of this contract and the fixture every test builds on. Its files are shown in the parts package README, `packages/fransys-parts/README.md`.

## Packaging and pinning

A part library is an ordinary Python data package: no build step beyond packaging the TOML
files, no Fransys code inside it.

- **Normal use.** A project pins the library as a git dependency with an exact
  revision: `co-parts = { git = "https://...", rev = "<sha>" }` in its `pyproject.toml`.
  `uv.lock` then pins the resolved commit, so a build needs no access to the library
  repository.
- **While authoring new parts.** The project instead points `[tool.uv.sources]` at a local
  checkout (`co-parts = { path = "../co-parts", editable = true }`), so edits to a part file are
  picked up without a commit and a re-pin. This is switched back to the git form before the
  change ships.
- `fransys_parts.lint` is meant to run in the library's own CI, so a bad part fails there and
  never reaches a project's build.

## Versioning

- `schema` (an integer, `1` today) is the part-file schema version, not the library's own `version`.
  A library can ship many releases against one `schema`.
- A breaking change to this contract (a renamed field, a changed meaning, a removed table) bumps
  `schema`. It is never changed in place under the same number.
- `fransys_parts.SUPPORTED_SCHEMAS: frozenset[int]` names the accepted `schema` values;
  today `frozenset({1})`. `library.toml` and every part file carry `schema`; a value outside
  `SUPPORTED_SCHEMAS` is the lint finding `SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`, naming the file and the value
  found, and a part file whose `schema` differs from its `library.toml` is `SCHEMA_MIXED`.
- There is no migration framework. A library bumps `schema` for every part file in one commit.

---

<!-- source: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.19.8/contracts/part-file-connectors/index.md -->

# Part-file contract: connectors

This page holds the `[function.connector]` table of the part-file contract. It is read with `part-file.md`, which holds the rest of the contract.

### `[function.connector]`

A sub-table of the `[[function]]` entry it describes (P1): the `connector` facet's subject is a
`FunctionTemplate`, not the `Part`, so a part with more than one connector-style function names
each one under its own `[[function]]` entry, never in one top-level table. Maps to the model's
`connector` facet.

```toml
[[function]]
name = "x1"
kind = "connector"
symbol = "connector-fixed"
ports = [{ name = "1", role = "generic", symbol_port = "in" }, { name = "2", role = "generic", symbol_port = "out" }]

[function.connector]
style = "header-2p"
pincount = 2
gender = "male"
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | string | |
| `pincount` | integer | At least 1 |
| `gender` | string | Optional. A `Gender` value: `"male"`, `"female"`, `"neutral"`. Absent means not stated, which is not `neutral` (model-0080) |
| `marking` | string | Optional. The label printed on the part, e.g. `"X1"`. Omit it to print the function's name; write `""` for no label, and the connector's pins print under the item |
| `mates` | list of strings | Optional. The MPNs of the parts this connector mates with, e.g. `["DEMO-HSG-4M"]`. Data only: no check reads it yet (parts-0016) |

Port names are unique within a function. Two functions of one part may share a port name unless
they would print one designation (`PORT_NAME_SHARED`, parts-0005): a labelled connector function
(its `marking`, else its name; `marking = ""` is no label) prints `-<label>` behind the item's
designation only when the part has two or more labelled connector functions, so `X1:1` and
`X2:1` differ, and so do a clamp group's `1` and `X1:1`, while a clamp group and a lone labelled
connector sharing `1` collide. The lint and the build ask the same segment rule
(`derive.connector_segments`). Two connectors of one part never print one label
(`CONNECTOR_MARKING_REUSED`). A pin prints as `-<item>-<label>:<pin>`, e.g. `-A1-X1:1` (decisions parts-0003, model-0071).

### A header pin that joins a function port

A port of a connector function may carry `joins = "<function>.<port>"`. It names a port of another function of the same part (parts-0017).

```toml
{ name = "1", role = "generic", symbol_port = "in", joins = "k1.A1" }
```

The header ports are named by position, `"1"` to `"n"`, and the printed pin text goes in `marking`. The join is stored once, on the header port's template. It is a connection with no conductor: net closure puts both ports on one net.

Three lints, all `ERROR`:
- `JOIN_PORT_UNKNOWN`: the target is no port of the part, or the value is malformed.
- `JOIN_INTO_CONNECTOR`: the target is a port of a connector function.
- `JOIN_PORT_TWICE`: one function port is joined by two header pins.

A header position that repeats another function's port name is `PORT_NAME_SHARED`.

### A contact part

A crimp contact is a part file with a `[part]` table and no `[[function]]`, as a fuse link is
(`DEMO-CRIMP-F`, `DEMO-CRIMP-M`). A design fits it with `contacts=` on a connector item
(`guide/harnesses.md`); the BOM counts it once per used pin (model-0170). It has no family or gauge
field yet.
